title: 8 Best call routing software for small businesses
summary: Looking for call routing software, but don’t know where to start? This guide covers the eight best call routing software options in depth.
body_text: When you were just starting to build your business, your call routing system may literally have been a personal cell phone and a call forwarding app. But times have changed, and now, call handling is more complex. You need to route calls across different locations, team members, devices, and departments. That’s why it’s important to choose call routing software that matches your current needs while giving you room to grow. You’re busy, so to save you time, we’ve put together a list of the best call routing software. We explain each platform’s features, pricing, and more so you can make an informed decision. Just want the TL;DR? Some of the best call routing software for businesses include: Quo, formerly OpenPhone: Best overall for small and growing businesses that want to keep scaling. Allo: Best for QuickBooks users. Five9: Best for large enterprises. Aircall: Best for brands that need international phone numbers. Comparing the best call routing software As you can guess, every business handles calls differently, so the best call routing software depends on how your team works and what features you need. That’s why the list below highlights the best call routing software for different business sizes, use cases, and routing options. But first, here’s a side-by-side look at the top providers. Providers Annual price Unlimited calls US/CA SMS and MMS Shared phone numbers Additional phone numbers Quo 15 per user per month ✔ ✔ ✔ $5 per number per month Aircall $30 ✔ ✔ ✗ $6 per number per month Allo $18 per month for one user ✔ 150 texts per number per day on all plans Requires upgrade $5 per number per month Dialpad $15 per user per month ✔ US & Canadian customers only ✔ Requires upgrade, then $5–$15 per month Nextiva $15 per user per month ✔ 100 SMS per user per month Requires upgrade Contact sales Five9 $119 per user per month Requires upgrade ✔ ✔ Contact sales Zendesk $55 per user per month Requires upgrade ✔ ✔ $1 per number per month Google Voice $10 US and Canadian numbers only US only ✗ ✗ Last updated July 2026 We’ll start with the platform rated #1 in customer satisfaction on G2: 1. Quo: Best for small and growing businesses Pros Call routing features are available on every plan Unlimited calls in Canada and the US Interactive voice response, or IVR, for inbound calls AI features like AI voice agent, call tags, call transcripts, and summaries Integrations with apps like Slack, HubSpot, and Salesforce Cons No verification through two-factor authentication* *Nearly all virtual phone numbers share this problem. Companies like Facebook, Uber, and Google rarely let you authenticate accounts through a virtual phone number. Quo is a business phone platform that offers call routing features on any plan. It helps growing small businesses set up flexible routing options that help ensure your team doesn’t miss calls. Every user you add to your Quo plan gets one local US, Canadian, or North American toll-free phone number. You also get access to unlimited calls and texts in the US and Canada, making it easy for your team to handle high call volumes. With Quo, you can set up time-of-day routing to send phone calls to different locations, depending on whether it’s during or after business hours. You might send daytime callers to reps who are currently available. For after-hours callers, you might forward them to an emergency number. Want to set up different call flows for weekend or holiday hours? Quo lets you create and toggle between multiple call flows based on what your team needs. You can also use Sona, an AI-powered voice agent that can answer calls 24/7. Route calls to Sona whenever your team is unavailable. It can answer FAQs, take messages, and even text during calls to save your team time with repetitive tasks like scheduling customer appointments. Sona can also transfer calls to your reps when the issue is too complex to solve on its own. On Quo’s Business plan, you can set up phone menus so callers automatically route themselves to the right rep or destination using their voice or phone keypad selections. You’ll also have access to ring groups. These allow you to customize which team members receive incoming calls and when. There are three different ring groups to choose from: All at once. Rings everyone on a shared phone number at the same time In random batches. Evenly distributes calls to your team in batches until someone picks up the phone Custom. Decide who gets incoming calls first and in what order Here’s what one customer had to say about using Quo: “I’ve finally found the unicorn phone system that does everything. Quo is extremely easy to use. We have a 6-person office routing calls to two companies, and the combination of simplicity and features is incredible.” — Sean Williams, Managing Director, Nymble Insurance Activate our call routing software in under 15 minutes. Try Quo for seven days by signing up for our free trial . Key features of Quo Warm and cold call transfers CRM integrations Call summaries and transcripts IVR call flows Custom ring orders Group calling Call recording Advanced call forwarding Shared phone numbers SMS auto-replies Quo pricing Quo’s pricing plans are designed to grow alongside your business. To get started, you can use call forwarding and shared numbers on our base plan. Then upgrade your plan for more features as you scale. Here’s what you can expect to get on each plan: Starter: $15 per user per month for unlimited domestic calling, call routing, voicemail and voicemail transcripts, call forwarding, call hold, Quo API , business hours, internal threads , Tasks, and more Business: $23 per user per month for advanced call forwarding, call transfers, IVR phone menus , custom ring orders, group calling, CRM integrations , live chat support, and more Scale: $35 per user per month for AI call tags , dedicated onboarding support, inbound phone support, and priority live chat and email support 2. Aircall: Best for buying international phone numbers Pros Local numbers in 100+ countries Unlimited calls within the US and Canada Call routing solutions like IVR and time-based routing Cons User minimums on every plan Smart routing, requires an upgrade Aircall is a global business phone system that supports local numbers in 100+ countries. It offers features like advanced call routing and ring groups to better distribute calls to international teams. You can use Aircall to create multi-level IVR menus that route callers to the right team, department, or location. For example, a caller can select a department first, then choose a specific location before being connected. Aircall also lets you set up time-of-day routing for both team and individual working hours. That way, callers are only routed to available reps instead of team members who’ve already finished for the day. But Aircall is more expensive than the other call routing software on this list. Its base plan costs $30 per user per month and comes with a three-user minimum. That means Aircall’s call routing features are a minimum of $90 per month. Plus, most of Aircall’s best routing features require one or more upgrades. The queue callback feature, for example, requires the Professional plan, which costs $50 per user per month. But considering that plan requires a three-user minimum, you’ll actually end up paying at least $150 per month. Key features of Aircall IVR support Queue callback, with an upgrade Time-based routing Mandatory call tagging, with an upgrade Call monitoring, with an upgrade Aircall pricing There are three Aircall pricing plans to choose from: Essentials: $30 per user per month for unlimited calls in Canada and the US, IVR system, call recording, click-to-dial, and SMS support, with a three-user minimum Professional: $50 per user per month for the Salesforce integration, mandatory call tagging, advanced analytics, and call monitoring, with a three-user minimum Custom: Custom price for unlimited calls worldwide and custom onboarding, with a 25-license minimum 3. Allo: Best for QuickBooks users Pros Conversational IVR is available Business hours routing Cons No shared numbers on the base plan Shopify and QuickBooks integrations require an upgrade Allo is a cloud-based VoIP system specifically designed for sales teams. It lets you set business hours, forward calls, and share phone numbers — although shared numbers require an upgraded plan. The base plan comes with conversational IVR . It uses natural language understanding, or NLU, so callers can speak in a natural way. This helps callers route to the correct rep or department faster, leading to better customer experiences. Own a Shopify store? Allo offers a Shopify integration that lets reps view a caller’s total orders, lifetime spending, and more during live calls. That way, reps have the context they need before answering customer questions. There’s also a QuickBooks integration that identifies callers before answering, then displays key customer information during the call. For example, reps can view outstanding invoices, total invoices, and lifetime revenue. This makes it easier to prioritize VIP customers and route billing-related questions to the right team or rep. But keep in mind these integrations require the Business plan, which costs $32 per user per month. Also, you can only send 150 text messages per number per day on all plans. Key features of Allo Business hours IVR routing Call forwarding Cascade ring SMS, with limits AI voice agent Allo pricing Allo’s pricing lets you choose between three plans. Here’s what you can expect to get on each: Starter: $18 per month for one user, unlimited calls in the US and Canada, business hours and IVR routing, Do Not Disturb mode, 150 SMS messages, and call recording Business: $32 per user per month for unlimited users, power dialer, call analytics, and shared inbox Ultra: $100 per user per month for custom analytics dashboards and custom AI voice for your IVR 4. Dialpad: Best for contact centers Pros Idle time call routing Digital contact center for multi-channel routing Cons AI agents cost $1,500 per year No additional numbers without upgrading Dialpad is a cloud communications platform specifically designed for contact centers. Unlike many other VoIP services, it offers idle time call routing. This tracks how active each rep has been throughout their shift and automatically routes calls to those who have been idle the longest. With Dialpad, you can easily create a digital contact center. It routes conversations to reps based on their channel expertise, like SMS and Instagram. That said, Dialpad doesn’t offer any additional phone numbers unless you upgrade your plan. This makes it harder to create separate routing options for different teams and locations. And some bare-bones features require add-ons. Want to route after-hours calls to an AI agent? Be prepared to pay at least an additional $1,500 per year, plus $1.99 per conversation handled by AI. Key features of Dialpad Custom call routing, including idle time call routing Custom phone menu greetings Call forwarding AI voice agent, with an add-on Ring groups, more are available with upgrades Dialpad pricing You have three Dialpad pricing plans to choose from: Standard: $15 per user per month for custom call routing, multi-level auto attendants, Dialpad SMS, voicemail transcriptions, call forwarding to other devices, three ring groups, and Google Workspace integrations Pro: $25 per user per month for hold queues, additional numbers, and 25 ring groups, with a three-user minimum Enterprise: Contact sales for 99.9% uptime, unlimited ring groups , SSO integration, and user access controls, with a 100-user minimum 5. Nextiva: Best for teams that use Microsoft products Pros Skills-based routing, with an upgrade or add-on Auto-attendant on the base plan Cons The MS Teams integration requires an upgrade or add-on Some users report issues with Nextiva’s call routing features Nextiva is an older VoIP platform that was established in 2006. In addition to business text messaging and video support, you can access different types of inbound call routing . This includes IVR routing, which lets you send calls through a phone menu before reaching a destination such as: Shared numbers Reps External phone numbers Recorded messages AI voice agent Nextiva also offers a Microsoft Teams integration. That way, you can make and receive calls directly from MS Teams using your Nextiva phone number. But this requires either a paid add-on on the base plan, with pricing not publicly available, or an upgrade to the Engage plan. This is almost double the cost at $25 per user per month. And keep in mind that some users report issues with this integration. See for yourself: “We are having issues with answering calls in Microsoft Teams—especially when users are part of a Nextiva call group.” — Microsoft’s Q&A forum Want your team to have a shared SMS inbox so they can send, receive, and manage customer text messages together? You’ll need to upgrade to the Engage plan first. What about improving first-call resolution by routing callers via skills-based routing? You’ll need to pay for the most expensive plan. This costs $75 per user per month. Not ready to spend that amount of money? You may want to choose a Nextiva alternative. Key features of Nextiva Auto-attendant Smart call routing, with an upgrade Inbound call handling Shared numbers and inboxes, with an upgrade Skills-based routing, with an upgrade Nextiva pricing You can choose from the following Nextiva pricing plans: Core: $15 per user per month for unlimited domestic calling, up to 100 SMS messages, auto-attendant, voicemail transcriptions, team messaging, and call routing Engage: $25 per user per month for an integration with Microsoft Teams, 500 SMS messages, 2,000 pooled toll-free minutes, and call recording Power Suite: $75 per user per month for skills-based routing, 10,000 pooled toll-free minutes, and call transcriptions and summaries 6. Five9: Best for large enterprises Pros ACD, or automatic call distribution Round robin features for call routing, with an upgrade Cons No voice calling on the base plan, requires an upgrade Nontransparent pricing Five9 is a cloud contact center for companies managing high call volumes. One of its biggest claims to fame is ACD, or automatic call distribution . This feature automatically distributes calls based on rep idle time, round robin, minimum calls handled, and more. That way, it’s easier to balance workloads across the team and prevent reps from cherry-picking certain calls. You can also use features like hold music and in-queue announcements to offer estimated wait times while callers wait for a rep. Not only does this help set clear expectations, but it can also help reduce abandoned calls . That said, voice calling isn’t available on Five9’s base plan. That means there are no call routing features available without upgrading to the Core plan. This works out to about $159 per user per month — although keep in mind, this requires a 50-seat minimum. Considering Five9’s call quality isn’t always up to par, it may be too high an investment for small and growing businesses. Here’s what one user had to say about Five9’s call routing and call quality: “I really like the intelligent call routing, which automatically directs calls to the most appropriate agent based on their skills and availability, … [but] sometimes the calls drop automatically, which is a direct financial loss.” — G2 Key features of Five9 Voice support, with an upgrade Automatic call distribution Round robin calls Hold music In-queue call announcements Five9 pricing Five9’s pricing is only partially transparent. You can only see prices for two out of five plans on its website. Here’s a quick breakdown of each: Digital: $119 per user per month for chat, SMS, email, and social messaging Core: $159 per user per month for voice support, IVR, call recording, the dialer, and AI transcripts and summaries Plus: Contact sales for additional artificial intelligence features, such as the AI Agent Assist and AI Knowledge Pro: Contact sales for a quote to access all the features of the Core and Digital plans, plus workforce engagement tools Enterprise: Contact sales for all features available on the Digital, Core, Plus, and Pro plans Keep in mind that these prices are based on concurrent users, meaning the number of team members who useFive9 at the same time. Five9 also requires a minimum of 50 seats. 7. Zendesk: Best for omnichannel routing Pros Intelligent omnichannel routing for calls, emails, and app messaging Call forwarding via Failover Cons No VoIP phone on the base plan No business hours on the two lowest-tier plans Zendesk is a customer service and sales platform offering omnichannel routing. This means it automatically directs calls, emails, and messages into one inbox and to the most suitable rep based on predefined rules. That way, your callers can reach the right person or department faster. You can also use Zendesk to forward calls to external phone numbers through a feature called Failover. Let’s say a customer calls your main business line, but there’s a power outage preventing you from receiving calls. Failover sends the caller to another number where you can continue providing support with minimal downtime. But since VoIP calling isn’t available on the base plan, call routing isn’t available either. You’ll have to upgrade to the Suite plan, which starts at $55 per user per month, just to use basic call routing features. You should also know business hours aren’t available on the two lowest-tier plans. The Suite Growth plan, which starts at $89 per user per month, is the only way to access it. Considering most VoIP systems offer these on the base plan, Zendesk may be too expensive for small and growing teams. Key features of Zendesk Omnichannel routing across email, chat, phone, social, and WhatsApp Call forwarding to external phone numbers Ticket routing Business hours 1,000+ integrations Zendesk pricing Zendesk’s pricing for phone support starts on the Suite Team. That said, you can technically choose from one of four plans: Support team: $19 per user per month for ticket routing, the ability to manage web chat, mobile, and social media conversations from a single inbox, integrations, and pre-written responses for incoming messages Suite Team: $55 per user per month for omnichannel routing to reps, voice support, queue size and wait times, and call recording Suite Professional: $115 per user per month for IVR, business hours, conference calling, request a callback, and the option to assign priority numbers Suite Enterprise + Copilot: Contact sales for AI Intelligent Triage so reps see what customers need when resolving tickets, automatic email archiving, skills-based routing, on-demand Failover, and extended queue size and wait time 8. Google Voice: Best for Google Workspace users Pros Ring groups with round robin distribution Call transfers are available Cons Requires Google Workspace to use with more than one user No AI voice agent is available Google Voice is a phone system that offers a free and a business version. The free version of Google Voice was built for individuals. Google Voice for business , on the other hand, offers the call routing features that growing brands need. Call transfers, for example, let you manually move callers to a specific rep or department. You can also play custom voicemail greetings to certain contacts. That way, it’s easier to offer VIP experiences to high-value or brand-new customers. Google Voice for business also supports ring groups with three tiers: Round robin to rotate calls evenly between team members Simultaneous ring to notify everyone at once of an incoming call Fixed order to ring team members in a predefined sequence until someone answers Keep in mind, Google Voice for business requires Google Workspace, which starts at $7 per user per month. So if you want more than one person on an account, you’ll need a Workspace subscription on top of your Voice plan. Plus, Google Voice doesn’t offer an AI voice agent to answer and route calls when your team is unavailable. This can lead to more missed opportunities after hours or during busy periods. If you’re looking for a tool that offers these features on the base plan, you may want to look for a Google Voice alternative . Key features of Google Voice Round robin call distribution Simultaneous ring Call transfers Custom voicemail greetings Call queueing Google Voice pricing There are a few Google Voice pricing plans you can choose from. Here’s what you can expect to get on each: Starter, Voice only: $10 per month for one user, unlimited calling and texting in the US, voicemail transcriptions, and three-way calling, only for US businesses Standard, Voice only: $20 per month for one user and auto attendants, only for US businesses Starter: $10 per user per month for three-way calling, call transfers, desk phone support, and call recording, for 10 users Standard: $20 per user per month for multi-level auto-attendants , ring groups, and call queueing, for unlimited users Premier: $30 per user per month for access to advanced reporting of Voice activity with BigQuery, automatic call recording, and the ability to get additional numbers outside of your home country Keep in mind, prices for Google Workspace start at $7 per user per month. Plans with more features, like additional storage, cost $22 per user per month. What is call routing? Call routing is a phone system feature that automatically directs incoming calls to the right person or team based on rules you set. Instead of every call going to the same place, your system decides where calls should go and what happens if nobody answers. Most businesses choose to create routing rules based on factors like: Business hours Team availability Regions and service areas Skills and specialties Departments You can also send calls to fallback options like emergency numbers, voicemail, or an AI voice agent like Quo’s Sona. What are the different types of call routing? Some of the most common types of call routing strategies include: Simultaneous ring. Multiple team members get notified about the same call at once. Time-of-day routing . Directs calls to different destinations based on the time of day. Shared number routing. Lets multiple users share the same phone number to route incoming calls to different reps. AI call routing. Routes incoming calls to an AI voice agent to answer questions and provide customer support. IVR call routing . Stands for interactive voice response, which lets people route themselves using their voices or keypad inputs. Round-robin routing. Equal call distribution so all reps have a chance to speak with customers. Shift-based routing. Route calls to available reps only, skipping reps who are unavailable. Skills-based routing. Matches callers to the rep best equipped to help them based on expertise. Sequential routing. Call reps in predetermined batches. When one isn’t available, your call routing software will call the next batch. How to choose the best call routing software Struggling to choose the right call routing software? To help narrow down your list, consider the following factors: Routing options. Not all call routing software works the same way. Some providers only offer basic call forwarding. Others support phone menus and visual call flow builders. Make sure the platform supports the routing options your team needs before signing on the dotted line. Team size. A small painting company may only need a shared number and basic ring groups. Larger enterprises may need advanced routing features like call queues and skill-based routing. Pricing. Pay close attention to which routing features are included in the base plan. Some providers lock features like business hours and voice calls behind higher-tier plans. Growth plans. Your routing needs will likely become more complex as your business grows. Look for software that can support your growth with intelligent call routing options. After-hours coverage. What can your phone system do when nobody’s available to answer? Some providers let you route calls differently during evenings, weekends, and holidays. Others offer AI voice agents that can answer calls, capture leads, and take messages when your team is unavailable. Quo: The best call routing software Call routing isn’t just for large enterprises with high call volumes. With Quo’s call routing software, it’s never been easier to set up a custom call flow for small and growing businesses. We offer IVR menus , business hours call routing , and shared phone numbers to help direct calls to the right people or departments. You can also answer the phone 24/7 with our AI voice agent, Sona. Plus, we offer thousands of integrations via Zapier and Make to save your team time. Sign up today for a seven-day free trial and test Quo’s call routing software with your team. FAQs What’s the difference between call routing and call forwarding? Call forwarding redirects incoming calls from one phone number to another. Call routing, on the other hand, uses rules you set to decide when and where to send calls. How long does it take to set up call routing? If you choose a business phone platform like Quo, you can set up call routing in 15 minutes or less. All you need to do is use the visual call flow builder to set up your call flows via your phone number settings. Create a basic flow by adding business hours, a phone menu, ring groups, and voicemail, then publishing it. Can I use my existing number with a new provider that offers better call routing options? Yes, you can port an existing number to a new provider that offers better call routing options. Here’s how to port over a local US, Canadian, or North American toll-free number with Quo: – Submit your port request. – Wait for us to receive confirmation from your carrier. – We’ll inform you of the scheduled port date and time. – Your phone number will be available in your Quo account at the scheduled time. – Once porting is confirmed, contact your old carrier to make sure your subscription is canceled. That’s it! How much does call routing software cost? That depends on the service you select. Quo, for example, starts at $15 per user per month. But some call center software can cost $150 per user per month or more. How does call routing software integrate with CRM systems? Quo lets you use CRM integrations, including HubSpot, Salesforce, Zoho, and Pipedrive, with your call routing software to: – Automatically log calls, texts, voicemails, and call summaries, giving your team a clear, single source of truth. – See when incoming calls from an existing customer saved as a CRM contact reaches out. – Click-to-call directly from your CRM using your Quo phone number.

title: Speed to Lead Automotive: 2026 Benchmarks, SLAs & Scripts
summary: Dealerships that respond within 15 minutes close 50% more leads. Get 2026 benchmarks, SLAs, templates, and a 30-day speed to lead automotive plan.
body_text: If you searched “speed to lead automotive,” you’re probably trying to fix one of these problems: internet leads go cold because the first real reply takes hours, your phones technically ring but customers hit hold or voicemail and disappear, your BDC looks busy all day but appointments aren’t improving, or after-hours and peak-time spikes are quietly destroying your connection rates. This guide is built as a complete operating manual, not a list of tips. We’re covering benchmarks from 2025-2026 research across thousands of dealerships, the SLAs you should actually be running in your store right now, ready-to-use templates that convert, and a realistic 30-day plan to deploy all of it. Whether you’re managing a single rooftop or a multi-store group, the mechanics here are the same. What Does Speed to Lead Mean in Automotive? Most people define speed to lead as “time from lead creation to first contact.” That’s a start, but it misses the point. In dealerships, speed to lead only matters when it creates speed to outcome . A lead is alive when two things are true at the same time: the customer still wants help, and they still believe your dealership is the easiest path to getting that help. The moment either of those breaks, the lead is functionally dead regardless of what your CRM says. The most important reframing is this: a dealership can “respond” and still miss the lead entirely. Picture this scenario. An auto-email goes out the instant someone submits a VDP form. Your CRM marks “responded within 5 minutes.” The customer asked “Is this vehicle available and what’s the out-the-door price?” The email says “Thanks for reaching out, we’ll contact you soon.” The customer buys elsewhere. That’s not speed to lead. That’s speed to disappointment. This is why modern research on lead responsiveness measures both speed and quality, not just timestamps. The Pied Piper ILE study specifically calls out “digital handoff risk,” where automation creates the illusion of coverage while the actual customer experience fails. Your dashboard can look clean while the customer is already at the next dealership. Dealership customer experience statistics confirm exactly how quickly customer intent evaporates when responses are slow or unhelpful. Speed to lead in automotive means: how long does it take you to move a customer from “shopping around” into a concrete next step — a scheduled appointment, a quote conversation, a confirmed test drive, or a warm transfer to the right person? Understanding what a BDC is in a car dealership and how it’s supposed to manage this process is the starting point for building a real speed-to-lead system. Why Speed to Lead Actually Works in Automotive Three basic mechanics explain why speed to lead matters. None of these are sales theory. They’re just how humans behave. Attention decays fast. When someone submits a form or calls your store, they’re at a local peak of intent. Every minute that passes, they either keep shopping and find a better path, or they emotionally cool off and stop wanting to deal with it today. Research from MIT and InsideSales.com found that waiting from 5 minutes to 30 minutes reduced the odds of contacting a lead by 100x and reduced qualifying odds by 21x. The exact multiplier probably differs in automotive, but the shape of the curve holds. Switching costs are near zero. If you don’t answer, the customer doesn’t have to break up with you. They just open another tab or dial the next store on Google Maps. There’s no loyalty at the research stage, and customers know it. Dealership customer experience statistics are unambiguous: once a customer reaches a competitor who answers, they rarely come back. The first helpful responder wins mindshare. Speed matters because it creates a perception: “This dealership is organized. They’re going to take care of me.” In automotive, where customers fully expect friction, removing friction feels like differentiation. It’s one of the easiest competitive edges you can build because most dealerships are still slow. AI follow-up systems now make it possible to be that first helpful responder around the clock, not just during business hours. 4 Dealership Lead Types and When the Clock Starts One of the biggest blind spots is treating all leads the same. They’re not. The clock starts at different moments, and the failure modes are completely different. -> Phone calls (sales and service): The clock starts when the phone rings. If the customer is on hold, the clock is still running. Car Wars phone performance data analyzed across nearly 3,000 dealerships found that the average hold time was 3 minutes and 5 seconds , and 31.8% of unconnected calls were customers hanging up while waiting on hold. That’s not a “response time” problem. That’s a failure-to-connect problem, and it’s expensive. The true cost of dealership hold times goes far beyond what most managers see in their dashboards. -> Website and internet leads: The clock starts at form submit. But “clock-stopper” emails that say nothing useful don’t count as contact in the customer’s mind. A 2025 Maritz FAQ for dealership teams explicitly flags clock-stoppers as outdated during business hours, noting they exist to satisfy OEM timing mandates rather than actually help customers. Tracking the right BDC metrics — specifically first helpful response time, not just first response time — is how you catch this gap. -> Third-party leads (CarGurus, KBB, OEM sites): The clock starts when the lead lands in your CRM. Speed here requires good plumbing underneath: the lead needs to land correctly, be owned by a specific person, and actually be worked. Many speed-to-lead failures on third-party leads aren’t about willingness, they’re about leads sitting in a queue nobody owns. An AI BDC solves this by ensuring every inbound touchpoint gets an immediate, substantive response without relying on a human to pick it up first. -> After-hours inquiries: The clock starts immediately, but your options change. Human coverage is expensive and hard to staff consistently. Automation and AI coverage works if it can actually complete the task (not just send an acknowledgement) and hand off cleanly when humans come back on. What matters is not “Did we send something?” It’s “Did the customer get what they needed without waiting until tomorrow?” Understanding when your dealership gets the most calls and mapping that against your current coverage reveals where your after-hours strategy is costing you most. Speed to Lead Benchmarks for Dealerships in 2026 You can’t manage what you don’t benchmark. Here are the most recent, dealership-specific data points to use as your starting line. Are Dealership Internet Lead Response Times Getting Better? The 2026 Pied Piper PSI Internet Lead Effectiveness study (the 15th year of the study) measured secret shopper inquiries across 3,290 franchise dealerships and scored speed plus quality across email, phone, text, and chat over 24 hours. Franchise dealers averaged a score of 71 out of 100 , a 6-point jump from 2025. Key results worth building into your own SLA thinking: 51% of dealers delivered a “perfect response” (answering the question through multiple channels including email, text, and phone) within 15 minutes Text usage to answer questions rose to 54% (from 38% in 2025) Phone calls rose to 75% (from 66% in 2025) 62% used both phone plus email/text , up from 49% the year before And the warning you shouldn’t ignore: when inquiries required human involvement, scores were 9 points lower and customers were twice as likely to receive no personal response at all. That’s the “digital handoff risk” problem in practice. Dealership customer experience statistics confirm that these handoff failures are among the most common reasons customers defect to competitors. Why 15-Minute Response Time Is Now the Dealership Standard DAS Technology released a nationwide study at NADA 2025 based on over 1,700 dealerships across Q3-Q4 2024. Their findings: 61% of dealerships responded within 15 minutes (up from 55% in 2022) and only 19% took over an hour. But the quality gaps are the real story. 91% excluded payment details. 74% didn’t offer price quotes. 89% included no alternative vehicle options. Speed is improving. Quality is not keeping pace. This is why tracking BDC metrics requires measuring response quality alongside response time. Raw timestamps tell you almost nothing about whether a lead was actually worked. What Top-Performing Dealer Groups Do Differently WardsAuto’s summary of the 2025 Pied Piper Dealer Group Study identified the pattern at top-performing dealer groups: respond via email or text within one hour, then follow up with a phone call ideally within 15 minutes. In the top-performing groups, 90% responded by email or text within an hour , 96% followed up by phone, and three-quarters of those calls happened within 15 minutes. The ROI implication is worth sitting with: improving ILE performance from below 40 to above 80 is associated with a 50% increase in unit sales from the same volume of website leads. You don’t need more leads. You need to work the ones you already have. AI follow-up systems can automate the multi-channel early-response sequence that drives this outcome, ensuring every lead gets the high-performer treatment without depending on rep availability. Why OEM Response Benchmarks Are Just the Starting Point Maritz points out that many dealers aim to hit OEM 30-minute response benchmarks, but the highest-performing dealerships combine speed with quality. OEM compliance is the floor. Your local market competitive position is the actual game. Understanding when your dealership gets the most calls gives you the data to staff and automate around your specific peak windows rather than generic industry averages. Speed to Lead SLAs Every Dealership Should Set in 2026 You need SLAs that reflect how customers actually behave and how your store actually operates. Below is a practical framework. Use it as a starting point and tighten it as your team proves they can hit it consistently. Phone Response SLAs for Sales and Service Level Answer Time Hold Time Minimum Within 60 seconds Under 2 minutes Competitive Within 20 seconds Under 60 seconds Top tier No hold for simple tasks Overflow path that still resolves the call The reason to be aggressive here: Car Wars’ call data shows the average hold time is over 3 minutes and that’s where a huge chunk of calls die. Hold is not neutral waiting time. It’s active abandonment risk. The true cost of dealership hold times goes well beyond the obvious. Every second of hold is eroding a buying relationship you already paid to generate. And why 32% of dealership callers hang up before they ever reach a human is the exact problem these SLAs are designed to solve. Internet Lead Response SLAs Level First Response Minimum Helpful first reply within 30 minutes Competitive Helpful first reply within 15 minutes Top tier Multi-channel attempt within 15 minutes (text or email plus a call when appropriate) “15 minutes” appears in multiple recent studies because it’s becoming the line between serious dealership and slow dealership in customers’ experience. To consistently hit multi-channel within 15 minutes for every internet lead, AI follow-up automation is the only reliable path at scale. Human teams can’t do it consistently across every shift, every day. After-Hours Lead Coverage SLAs Level Standard Minimum Immediate acknowledgement with a specific next step and a promised callback time Competitive Immediate helpful response that answers questions and books the appointment if possible Top tier Full 24/7 task completion: book, confirm, update, route If you can only make one after-hours improvement this quarter, make it this: turn “we’ll call you tomorrow” into “you’re booked.” That single change closes the biggest speed-to-lead gap most dealerships still have. Automating service appointment scheduling at the after-hours level is where the ROI is clearest: you’re capturing appointments that currently go to voicemail and die. How to Build a Speed to Lead System That Actually Works If your plan is “tell reps to respond faster,” you’ll get a short spike and then decay back to baseline. That’s how motivation works. A real speed-to-lead system has five parts: Capture — every lead lands somewhere reliable Route — the right lead gets to the right owner instantly Engage — the first response answers the question and offers a next step Persist — follow-up continues long enough to match real buying timelines Cover — you don’t collapse after hours or during peak periods Here’s how each piece becomes concrete. Step 1: Audit Your Real Response Time (Not Your CRM’s) Most dealership dashboards measure activity, not customer experience. Pied Piper explicitly warns that breakdowns often don’t show up in CRM dashboards because the system can log activity even when the customer got no real answer. Run this audit today: pull 20 fresh leads across sources (OEM, VDP, third-party). For each one, answer when it arrived, when the customer received their first helpful answer, whether a next step was offered, whether a second channel was tried within an hour, and whether the customer was forced to repeat themselves. Do this once a week for a month. The BDC metrics every dealership should track make this audit systematic rather than a one-off exercise. Step 2: Define What a Valid First Response Actually Looks Like A first response only counts if it does at least one of the following: Answers the specific question asked Confirms availability with a clear next step Offers two specific appointment times Asks exactly one clarifying question that unlocks the next step Warm-transfers to the right department with context What doesn’t count: “Thanks for reaching out,” “We’ll contact you soon,” or “What’s the best time to call?” asked as a stall rather than a real scheduling offer. DAS Technology’s research confirms that most responses still omit core buying information like price quotes and payment details. Fast is wasted if it’s vague. Improving your CSI scores is directly tied to this: customers who get helpful, substantive first responses have dramatically better satisfaction scores. Step 3: Build a Lead Routing Model That Matches Your Reality Most speed-to-lead failures aren’t caused by lazy reps. They’re caused by leads landing in a place where nobody owns them. To fix this, you need three things. First, a single owner per lead — not “the sales team,” not “the internet department,” but a specific person or a named queue with a manager accountable for it. Second, a fast path for high-intent leads: phone calls (especially service), trade-in value requests, “in stock” vehicle questions, and appointment requests are the closest to action and should get priority routing. Third, a clean overflow rule. Car Wars data shows Monday 10am to 12pm is consistently your highest-traffic window . If you don’t have an overflow plan, your peak demand will always be when you respond slowest. Call overflow solutions turn a reactive routing model into a proactive one. Step 4: Automate the Multi-Channel Response Sequence Decide once, bake it in, and stop thinking about it. Use the dealer-group formula from Pied Piper’s 2025 work : email or text within one hour, phone call ideally within 15 minutes. Then compress that window as much as your store can sustain. The industry shift in 2026 is toward multi-channel early, not single-channel late. AI follow-up automation is how high-performing groups operationalize this without burning out their teams. The sequence runs automatically regardless of who’s in the building. Step 5: Fix After-Hours and Peak-Time Coverage Gaps There are two consistent speed traps in every dealership. After-hours: if you wait until tomorrow morning, you’re competing against every dealership that actually responded the night before. And peak-time spikes: the window when the store is busiest is also the window when customers are most likely to hit hold and give up. Car Wars phone data makes the cost of this explicit . Solving both requires either better staffing models, overflow coverage, or technology that can handle the volume when humans can’t. A virtual receptionist for car dealerships is increasingly how forward-thinking stores handle after-hours and peak-time coverage without scaling headcount. Dealership Response Scripts and Templates That Convert The goal of these templates isn’t to be clever. It’s to remove friction. Copy, adapt, and deploy. Template 1: First text message (sales lead) Hi [first_name], this is [rep_name] at [dealership]. Yes, [vehicle] is available right now. Quick question so I can give you the most accurate numbers: are you paying cash, financing, or leasing? Why this works: it answers the availability question, asks one clarifying question that unlocks the next step, and doesn’t ramble. Two sentences of actual value beat three paragraphs of pleasantries. Template 2: First email (sales lead) Subject: [Vehicle] availability + next steps Yes, it’s available as of [time]. Two options to move this forward today: Option A: I send you numbers (cash, finance, or lease) Option B: I hold a time for you to see it (today at [time1] or [time2]) One question: cash, finance, or lease? Template 3: Service scheduling request Thanks for reaching out. I can book your service appointment. What are we working on, and what day works best? If you tell me “weekday mornings” or “after 5pm,” I’ll give you two specific time options. This sets the expectation that booking is happening (not “I’ll have someone call you”), moves directly to appointment logistics, and still collects the info needed. For automating service appointment scheduling at scale, this conversational pattern is what AI handles most effectively. Template 4: Missed call recovery text Hi [first_name]. Sorry we missed you. I can help now. What were you calling about: service, sales, parts, or something else? The goal is simple: get them back into a live thread. A live recovery text like this, sent within seconds of a missed call, recovers a significant portion of leads that would otherwise be lost to a competitor. Why dealership voicemails kill sales explains why this step is so high-leverage. The Speed to Lead Scoreboard Every Dealership Should Run If you want speed to lead to stick, track it the same way you track gross and CSI. Here are the metrics that matter. For sales: Median time to first helpful response (by lead source) Percentage of leads touched within 15 minutes Percentage of leads touched within 60 minutes Contact rate (two-way conversations divided by total leads) Appointment set rate Appointment show rate Close rate from kept appointments For service: Average speed to answer Average hold time Abandon rate (hang-ups before resolution) Voicemail rate Appointment set rate from calls Mission failure rate (caller didn’t get an appointment or resolution) Speed affects contact, contact affects appointments, and appointments are where revenue happens. If you’re only tracking “first response time,” you’re watching the first domino and ignoring everything after it. BDC metrics every dealership should track covers this full chain in detail and explains how to build a scoreboard so managers can see the truth rather than just activity. For service-specific tracking, how AI is transforming dealership service departments shows what top-tier visibility looks like when every call and booking is automatically logged. 30-Day Speed to Lead Implementation Plan for Dealerships Here’s how to deploy this without blowing up your team. Days 1-3: Baseline and plumbing Pull the last 14 days of lead timestamps and first-response timestamps. Identify your top three lead sources by volume and by close rate. Find your “speed trap” hours (start with Monday 10am to 12pm). Fix routing ownership gaps where leads land in a shared inbox or unassigned queue. When your dealership gets the most calls is your baseline for where routing failures cost you most. Days 4-10: SLAs and scripts Publish SLAs by channel so everyone knows what “good” looks like. Write your first-response templates based on the frameworks above. Train the team on the difference between a “helpful response” and a “clock stopper” — Maritz makes clear most teams don’t actually know the difference. Connect BDC metrics to your new SLAs so the scoreboard reflects what you’re asking the team to hit. Days 11-20: Multi-channel and persistence Make multi-channel outreach the default for high-intent leads — not something reps do when they feel like it. Add a follow-up cadence that extends well beyond 24 hours. Maritz notes that buyers convert much later than most teams expect, which means follow-up length directly affects deals closed. How AI follow-up helps dealerships close more leads explains how to build persistence without burning out your team. Days 21-30: Coverage and stress testing Mystery shop yourself weekly. Stress test the phones by calling three lines at once during your peak window. Fix after-hours coverage for one specific use case — service scheduling is usually the cleanest place to start. Automating service appointment scheduling is the highest-volume use case where 24/7 automation produces the clearest ROI. Call overflow solutions address the parallel challenge during peak hours. Speed to Lead Mistakes Most Dealerships Make Even dealerships with good intentions get stuck on these three patterns. Trap 1: Celebrating fast replies that don’t answer the question. Your customers don’t care that your CRM clock stopped. They care that you helped. DAS Technology’s research found that even as response times improve, most dealers still fail to include price quotes, payment details, or alternative vehicle options in their first response. Faster vague replies are still losing leads. Dealership customer experience statistics document this gap in detail. Trap 2: Assuming automation solves handoffs. Automation helps significantly, but Pied Piper’s 2026 study highlights what they call “digital handoff risk” — where system-to-system failures and AI-to-human transitions create hidden breakdowns. The customer submits a form, automation fires, a human is supposed to follow up, the handoff breaks, and the customer gets nothing. The fix is to measure outcomes, not activity. Did the customer get an appointment? Did they get their question answered? Those are the only metrics that matter. What is an AI BDC and how it automates dealership calls explains how properly designed AI systems handle handoffs differently from rule-based automation. Trap 3: Ignoring phone leads because “internet is everything.” A phone call is often your highest-intent lead. If customers are hanging up on hold, your marketing dollars are literally paying to generate calls you don’t convert. Car Wars’ analysis of nearly 3,000 dealerships should remove any doubt: nearly a third of callers abandon on hold , and 32% end up in voicemail. These are not people who didn’t want to buy. They’re people you didn’t get to in time. Why 32% of dealership callers hang up and what to do about it is one of the highest-impact improvements most dealerships can make this quarter. How Flai Solves the Speed to Lead Problem for Dealerships Everything in this guide points to the same structural challenge: dealerships have predictable, recurring windows where leads arrive and humans can’t keep up. After hours. Peak-time spikes. Monday mornings. Service scheduling surges. The fix isn’t hiring more BDC reps for every conceivable scenario. It’s building a system that’s already working when the customer tries to reach you. That’s what Flai is built to do. It’s an AI communications platform built specifically for car dealerships , functioning as a 24/7 AI BDC that handles every inbound call, text, and email regardless of time of day or call volume. When a customer reaches out at 10pm on Sunday or during a Monday morning spike when every phone line is ringing, Flai picks up, has a real conversation, and books the appointment directly into the scheduler. Not a voicemail. Not a message for someone to call back. An actual booked slot. The key distinction is integration depth. Flai connects directly to your DMS, CRM, and scheduler, which means it can check real availability and confirm a booking in the same conversation. This is why the conversion numbers from actual Flai deployments are meaningful rather than theoretical. A Lexus dealership in the Bay Area went from zero after-hours coverage to handling approximately 1,100 calls with zero missed , converting 88% of bookable calls to appointments , and generating roughly $100,000 in monthly profit impact . A CDJR dealership in the same region saw monthly service appointments jump from 205 to 448 in the first month , with Flai booking 304 of those appointments and contributing approximately $83,000 in profit impact in 30 days. Consider the statistic that 56-60% of dealership leads arrive after business hours. And that roughly 70% of people who hit voicemail call a competitor within about 30 minutes. If your after-hours coverage is a voicemail box, you’re not just slow. You’re handing that business to the next store in their search results. Replacing outsourced call centers with AI is the strategic shift that closes this gap permanently. Unlike outsourced services, AI actually books the appointment rather than just taking a message. Flai also handles the peak-time overflow problem. During your Monday 10-12 spike, when your human team is at capacity and calls start going to hold, Flai acts as call overflow coverage that resolves calls rather than just taking messages. Warm transfers happen with context (not blind transfers that force customers to repeat themselves). Follow-up on sales leads happens via phone, text, and email as real two-way conversations. Beyond coverage, Flai gives you visibility. Every call handled, every appointment booked, every outcome logged. So instead of guessing what your Monday 10-12 connection rate looks like, you can see it. This is the kind of data that makes BDC performance tracking actionable rather than theoretical. If the question you want to be able to answer “yes” to is “when a customer reaches out, do they feel like we’re the easiest path to getting it done?”, Flai is how you make that true around the clock. Book a demo to see exactly how it works at a store like yours. Frequently Asked Questions What’s the ideal response time for dealership internet leads? Based on the most recent 2026 research, 15 minutes is the competitive benchmark for a helpful first response to website and internet leads. The Pied Piper ILE 2026 study found that 51% of franchise dealers achieved a “perfect response” within 15 minutes. DAS Technology’s analysis found 61% responding within that window. Under 15 minutes for a substantive, helpful response is competitive. Over 30 minutes, you’re losing to dealerships that are faster. Tracking BDC metrics by lead source shows you exactly where your current performance falls relative to these benchmarks. Why do dealerships lose so many phone leads? Car Wars’ analysis across nearly 3,000 dealerships found that 31.8% of unconnected callers hang up while on hold , the average hold time is over 3 minutes , and 32.3% of non-connected calls go to voicemail. These aren’t customers who changed their minds. They’re customers who ran out of patience before reaching a human. The biggest fix is reducing or eliminating hold for simple tasks like service scheduling and general questions. Why 32% of dealership callers hang up gives a full breakdown of root causes and specific fixes organized by impact. How should dealerships handle after-hours leads? At minimum, after-hours inquiries need an immediate acknowledgement with a specific promised callback time (not just “we’ll call you”). Competitively, the response should answer questions and book the appointment if possible. Top tier is full 24/7 task completion: booking, confirming, updating records, and routing to the right person when staff return. Research shows roughly 56-60% of dealership leads arrive outside business hours , so this window isn’t a minor edge case. It’s where a majority of leads first try to reach you. A virtual receptionist for car dealerships is the most scalable solution for full 24/7 task completion without expanding your human team. How does AI help dealerships improve speed to lead? AI tools like Flai solve the structural problem that human staffing can’t solve: coverage during after-hours windows and peak-time spikes. An AI BDC answers every call and message immediately regardless of time, has real conversations, books appointments directly into the scheduler, and hands off to humans with context when needed. This eliminates the two biggest speed-to-lead gaps in most stores: after-hours black holes and peak-period hold abandonment. The practical effect isn’t theoretical. Flai deployments at real dealerships show 88% conversion rates on bookable calls and $80,000-$100,000+ in monthly profit impact per rooftop. Review the full case studies to see results from specific dealership types. How to Build a Dealership Customers Keep Coming Back To Speed to lead isn’t a metric to optimize in isolation. It’s a proxy for something bigger: whether your dealership feels organized, responsive, and worth doing business with. Customers shopping for a car or booking a service appointment are running a quick mental test. They reach out, they see how fast and helpfully you respond, and they decide whether you’re the kind of operation they trust with a purchase that might be tens of thousands of dollars. The dealerships winning on speed to lead in 2026 aren’t doing anything exotic. They’ve defined their SLAs, trained their teams on what a real first response looks like, built overflow coverage for the hours where humans can’t keep up, and started measuring outcomes instead of just activity. When a customer reaches out to your dealership, do they feel like you’re the easiest path to getting it done? That’s the only question that matters. Build your answer around it. title: How AI is Revolutionizing the CNC Machining Industry
summary: Welcome to Hurco! Around here, we believe that any machining problem is solvable when you pair the right tools with the right thinking.
body_text: How AI is Revolutionizing the CNC Machining Industry The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into the CNC machining industry is rapidly transforming the way manufacturers design, produce, and optimize their operations. AI-powered solutions are enhancing precision, reducing waste, improving efficiency, and driving innovation across the sector. In this article we will explore how AI is being utilized in CNC machining and what the future holds for this evolving technology. Process Optimization One of the most significant applications of AI in CNC machining is smart automation and process optimization. Traditional CNC machines rely on pre-programmed instructions and manual oversight, but AI enables them to self-optimize through real-time data analysis. Machine learning algorithms analyze historical and live data to optimize cutting speeds, feed rates, and tool paths, leading to more efficient machining with reduced cycle times. At Hurco, we are beginning to capture this data within the control for use in the future. We hope to apply this technology to help automate machining processes and make machining and conversational programming more efficient. Predictive Maintenance Preventative maintenance schedules used to help reduce downtime are very important, and AI-driven predictive maintenance is revolutionizing machine reliability. Instead of relying on scheduled maintenance or reactive repairs, AI monitors the condition of CNC machines through sensor data and performance analytics. By detecting wear and potential failures before they occur, manufacturers can schedule maintenance proactively, minimizing unexpected downtime and extending machine life. Obviously, it is much easier and less detrimental to plan for machine downtime in the manufacturing schedule instead of reacting to it when something happens, and the machine is completely down until repairs can be made. Enhanced Inspection Systems Quality assurance is crucial in CNC machining, and AI-powered inspection systems are enhancing accuracy. AI-driven vision systems use high-resolution cameras and machine learning algorithms to detect defects, inconsistencies, and deviations from specifications in real time. These automated inspection solutions provide faster and more precise quality control than human inspectors, ensuring higher consistency in production. Here at Hurco, we have a few of our customers who use this technology, and the speed at which these vision systems can evaluate data and react when something is out of spec is truly amazing. CAM Assist Tools With the introduction of products like CAM-Assist by Cloud NC, AI is also transforming the way we program using CAD/CAM software. AI-driven CAD/CAM tools assist engineers in optimizing designs for manufacturability, suggesting the best machining strategies and automatically generating toolpaths. These AI enhancements reduce programming time, improve part quality and streamline production workflows. Notably, AI-powered CAM assist tools in software such as Mastercam and Fusion 360 are helping machinists by automating toolpath generation, optimizing cutting strategies, and providing real-time recommendations, making programming more efficient and intuitive. Future of CNC Machining The future of AI in CNC machining is exciting. As AI technology continues to evolve, we can expect even more advancements in CNC machining. The development of autonomous machining systems, where AI handles the entire production process with minimal human intervention, is on the horizon. Additionally, AI-powered digital twins — virtual replicas of CNC machines and manufacturing processes — will enable manufacturers to simulate and optimize operations before physical production begins. AI is reshaping the CNC machining industry by enhancing automation, predictive maintenance, quality control, adaptive machining, and supply chain optimization. As AI continues to advance, manufacturers that embrace this technology will gain a competitive edge in efficiency, precision, and innovation.

title: Gestire i dati in modo più semplice e intuitivo con Comscore Total Digital
summary: Per la prima volta Comscore Total Digital permette a marketer, editori e centri media di accedere ad attività di misurazione su piattaforme digitali tradizionali e di social media da un'unica piattaforma intuitiva. Scopri alcuni dei dati destinati a semplificare le tue modalità di lavoro, grazie anche...
body_text: Per la prima volta Comscore Total Digital permette a marketer, editori e centri media di accedere ad attività di misurazione su piattaforme digitali tradizionali e di social media da un'unica piattaforma intuitiva. Scopri alcuni dei dati destinati a semplificare le tue modalità di lavoro, grazie anche alla visualizzazione grafica. Acquisisci una visione d’insieme delle audience digitali Comscore Total Digital rileva la composizione demografica delle tue audience digitali e di quelle dei concorrenti per un benchmarking più rapido. Prendendo come esempio il celebre marchio di cuffie Beats by Dre, possiamo constatare che il brand ha una audience di base costituita per l'84,9% da uomini e le fasce di età di almeno 35 anni sono quelle preponderanti. Le metriche di social engagement per Facebook, Instagram e Twitter forniscono ulteriori informazioni sulle performances, ripartite in base alla piattaforma. Nel mese di aprile, Beats by Dre contava una media di 103.600 actions2 su queste tre piattaforme di social media (+73,7% rispetto a marzo 2022), con Twitter che registrava l'incremento più significativo (+98,1%) e Instagram al primo posto in termini di engagement (92.200 actions). La rappresentazione grafica dei dati ci permette di identificare tendenze che chiariscono come le caratteristiche demografiche della property siano cambiate nel corso del tempo: nel caso della rivista Bustle, per esempio, notiamo che l’audience primaria continua a essere costituita da persone di 25-34 anni, anche se si evidenzia una crescita in numerose fasce di età nel corso dello stesso periodo temporale. Durante il semestre conclusosi ad aprile 2022, Bustle ha registrato un picco nell'engagement da parte di Millennial e Generazione Z, come mostrato di seguito: Analizza le tue principali piattaforme di social media Comscore Total Digital fornisce anche valori percentuali su audience, contenuti e actions per ciascuna piattaforma di social media. Queste metriche permettono di rivelare le piattaforme a cui la tua audience dedica un tempo maggiore, chiarendo anche dove si concentra il volume più consistente di contenuti e quali piattaforme generano i più alti livelli di engagement. Esaminando l'esempio della banca statunitense Capital One, notiamo che la maggior parte dei contenuti si concentra su Twitter (56,18%), mentre Facebook conta la fetta di audience più consistente. In termini di engagement, è però Instagram a piazzarsi nettamente in pole position (55,59% di engagement a fronte del 24,72% di contenuti). Identifica le "personas" con i maggiori livelli di engagement Per comprendere la diversità di una audience a un livello più approfondito, Comscore Total Digital permette di identificare anche le principali "personas" (o categorie di utenti), accompagnate dai relativi indici1. Nel caso dell'azienda di videogiochi Activision Blizzard, possiamo constatare che le principali categorie di utenti sono rappresentate da consumatori di alcolici, utenti fedeli al brand e appassionati di cultura pop. Ad esempio, vediamo che i consumatori di alcolici hanno un indice pari a 153,76, che significa che avranno il 54% di probabilità in più di interagire con Activision Blizzard sui social media rispetto all'utente medio. Inoltre, è possibile comprendere le relazioni esistenti tra una categoria e l'altra mettendo in evidenza eventuali sovrapposizioni. I dati rappresentati graficamente (come nell'esempio sottostante) possono aiutare i brand a mettere a punto campagne di influencer marketing ancora più mirate, o a identificare nuove opportunità per espandere la propria reach. Ottimizza con la Source/Loss Analysis Comscore Total Digital permette anche di ottenere visibilità sul traffico in entrata e in uscita da/verso una property, compreso il traffico correlato a piattaforme di social media. In questo modo sarai in grado di identificare gli altri siti web visitati dagli utenti prima/dopo essere approdati sul tuo sito. Ad esempio, nel caso di Crunchyroll, una piattaforma di streaming dedicata agli anime, il 13,65% della audience proviene da Google Sites, mentre l'11,30% accede al sito di Crunchyroll dopo aver aperto il browser. Ottieni una visione approfondita dei contenuti più performanti I dati relativi ai contenuti di social media, accessibili da Comscore Total Digital, permettono di identificare i post di tendenza e le principali keyword associate al tuo brand. Nello specifico, da qui è possibile visualizzare i post e le parole chiave che generano i più alti livelli di engagement per la tua audience, per aiutarti a ottimizzare i contenuti nel modo più efficace. Nel caso di Macy's, iconico grande magazzino di New York, notiamo immediatamente che i post di tendenza e i contenuti più performanti per il mese di aprile 2022 sono concentrati su Facebook. Osservando le keyword più ricercate, invece, rileviamo che la parola "stile" è quella che riesce a generare i maggiori livelli di engagement. Scopri chi sono i tuoi principali brand affini Comscore Total Digital mette a disposizione un elenco dei principali "brand affini", per acquisire informazioni sul grado di affinità e sull'engagement multi-piattaforma esistente a livello dei singoli brand (e dunque non delle sole categorie di interesse). Un valore di affinità superiore a dieci indica un elevato engagement multi-piattaforma tra due property sui social media. Nel caso del retailer statunitense Lowe’s, ad esempio, possiamo constatare che gli utenti che interagiscono con altri brand appartenenti alla stessa categoria (come Land’s End, Vici, Craftsman e Dyson) hanno maggiori probabilità di interagire con Lowe's rispetto all'utente medio. Ma livelli di affinità simili sono evidenti anche tra agli utenti che interagiscono con il Nationwide Children’s Hospital (un ospedale pediatrico di Columbus, Ohio), segnalando un potenziale interessante per la creazione di campagne ad hoc. L'accesso a informazioni sui brand affini permette di scoprire quali sono le aziende concorrenti in cui si evidenziano sovrapposizioni tra gli interessi dei membri delle rispettive audience, contribuendo a identificare nuovi target per campagne o partnership future. Per provare tutto questo dalla prospettiva del tuo brand, prenota una demo qui scegliendo la data e l'ora che preferisci . 1 Tutti gli indici hanno un valore base di 100. 2 Actions: Numero complessivo di azioni (reazioni, condivisioni, commenti, retweet, aggiunta ai preferiti, mi piace) ricevute dalla property durante un periodo predefinito nell'ambiente combinato di Facebook, Twitter e Instagram.
