title: Key Differences Between Centralized and Distributed Control Systems in Vehicle Design
summary: Learn about the key differences between centralized and distributed systems in vehicle designs and some key consideration
body_text: Distributed CAN modules reduce downtime in mobile equipment systems by eliminating single points of failure, enabling fault isolation, and improving overall system reliability. The difference between centralized and distributed control systems in vehicle design are how they control power and manage operations across multiple modules. This provides faster response time, greater efficiency and enhanced fault tolerance. We will dive deeper into each contrast and when to implement them into your next project. Key Difference The main differences between the two architectures determine everything from a vehicle’s safety and overall functions. Wiring Complexity and Weight Centralized: This requires wire across the entire system to connect all sensors and actuators to the central hub. The heavy wiring harness reduces fuel efficiency and range. Distributed: Localized modules connected to devices will communicate back to the main system like a data bus, while reducing weight. Tolerance and Safety Centralized: Operates with a single point of failure Distributed: Highly fault-tolerant for any localized controller fails, while the rest of the vehicle remains completely operational. Power and Scalability Centralized: Scales well for software updates and processing massive data. Distributed: Processing burdens are shared. Response Time Centralized: Slower for micro-second Distributed: Higher response time for real-time applications. Key Design Considerations CAN J1939 Communication offers high-speed communication for faster execution of vital processes and faster analysis of microprocessor unit messages, especially in large vehicles used in transportation, agriculture and industrial settings. Modular architecture supports specialized hardware modules that communicate via CAN bus and provides easier system scaling. Diagnostic Proper architecture ensures healthy system health and performance. Summary of Suitability Depending on the specific use of vehicle design, both centralize and decentralized control modules provides their own power system reliability.

body_text: Finding the right people is harder than it looks. Job boards overflow with applications, hiring managers drown in resumes, and strong candidates often accept offers elsewhere before a second interview is even scheduled. Recruitment Automation Tools have reshaped how companies approach this challenge, helping teams move faster, reduce bias, and focus energy on the candidates most likely to succeed. A smarter hiring process does not stop at the offer letter. Onboarding, role clarity, and early engagement all determine whether a new hire stays long enough to make a real contribution. Companies that treat recruitment and retention as a connected system, rather than separate problems, consistently build stronger teams, and that starts with a reliable global HR system . At the same time, 63% of employers identify skills gaps as the biggest barrier to business transformation, and nearly 40% of skills required for today's roles are expected to change by 2030. Reactive hiring, where recruitment begins only when a seat becomes vacant, cannot keep pace with that rate of change. Candidate experience has become a measurable competitive factor. Up to 80% of applicants abandon applications because of lengthy or unclear processes, and 64% of HR professionals say finding qualified talent has become harder even as applicant volumes grow. More applications do not automatically mean better fits, and organizations still optimizing for volume rather than match quality are losing candidates who have real options elsewhere. Skills-based hiring is gaining traction as a more reliable signal of a candidate's capabilities than credentials or linear career history. LinkedIn's Future of Recruiting 2025 report found that 93% of talent acquisition professionals believe accurately assessing candidate skills is essential to improving hire quality, and organizations conducting the most skills-based searches are 12% more likely to make a quality hire. This approach also reduces unconscious bias by tying evaluation criteria to demonstrated ability rather than background markers. Slow hiring timelines carry a direct competitive cost. It takes an average of 44 days to hire a new employee according to Cisive's 2025 hiring challenges report, and a bad hire can cost up to 30% of that employee's first-year earnings. In fast-moving talent markets, process delays are not a neutral operational fact; they are a signal to candidates about how an organization functions. Regional hiring in MENA adds layers of complexity that a single unified strategy rarely accounts for. In the UAE and Saudi Arabia, Emiratisation and Saudisation programs carry real financial consequences for organizations that miss targets, and both countries have enacted Personal Data Protection Laws that govern how candidate information is collected and stored during recruitment. LinkedIn's Future of Recruiting 2025 MENA report also found that 62% of recruiters in the region report difficulty finding qualified candidates, making process speed and clarity more important, not less. Recruitment data fragmented across disconnected tools makes it nearly impossible to improve hiring quality over time. Without visibility into which sourcing channels produce candidates who pass interviews and stay beyond their first year, investment gets allocated by habit rather than evidence. Cercli's global HR system addresses this by consolidating recruitment, onboarding, payroll, and analytics into a single, connected platform, so that candidate information flows automatically and hiring teams can make decisions based on data. Why Corporate Recruitment Strategies Need to Evolve Corporate recruitment has changed dramatically . The talent market is shaped by ongoing skills shortages , rising candidate expectations , and rapid change . According to HR Lineup's Recruitment Statistics Every HR Should Know in 2025 , 76% of employers report talent shortages at an all-time high , pushing businesses to expand hiring beyond traditional borders . " 76% of employers report talent shortages at an all-time high, pushing businesses to expand hiring beyond traditional borders." — HR Lineup, 2025 🚨 Warning: Companies that fail to evolve their recruitment strategies risk falling behind in an increasingly competitive talent landscape . The shortage is not a temporary trend. 🔑 Takeaway: A 76% talent shortage rate signals that traditional hiring approaches are insufficient. Businesses must rethink their recruitment models to stay competitive and attract top-tier candidates in a shrinking talent pool. Why is the hiring process itself the biggest failure point? The failure point is usually the process itself, not the pipeline. Today, 63% of employers say skills gaps are the biggest barrier to business transformation, according to the World Economic Forum's Future of Jobs Report 2025 , and nearly 40% of the skills required for today's roles are expected to change by 2030. Reactive hiring cannot keep pace with this change. Candidate expectations have shifted sharply. Job seekers now evaluate employers by researching culture, assessing values, and forming opinions before applying. Research from LinkedIn's 2025 talent report found that 64% of HR professionals say finding qualified talent has become harder, even as applicant volumes grow. The result: more applications, fewer fits . How do complex processes cause qualified candidates to disappear? Most teams respond by adding steps: more screening rounds, longer job descriptions, extra approvals. LinkedIn's research on candidate drop-off shows that up to 80% of applicants abandon applications due to lengthy or unclear processes. A global HR system like Cercli consolidates hiring workflows, candidate management, and onboarding into a single connected platform, eliminating gaps where qualified candidates can disappear between stages. What separates organizations that consistently win at talent acquisition? The organizations winning at talent acquisition treat recruitment as a continuous business function rather than a reactive response to open headcount. According to LinkedIn's Future of Recruiting 2025 report , 93% of talent acquisition professionals believe that accurately assessing candidate skills is essential to improving hire quality, and organizations that conduct the most skills-based searches are 12% more likely to make a quality hire. Recruitment strategy and business strategy are no longer separate conversations. Workforce planning, employer branding, skills-based hiring, and recruitment analytics all feed into the same outcome: building a team capable of delivering on business needs. Winning organizations build talent pipelines before they need them, use data to understand what drives successful hires, and invest in candidate experience as seriously as customer experience. Knowing your strategy needs to evolve is only half the answer. The harder question is which specific approaches move the needle. When one part is weak , the whole system slows down . "A corporate recruitment strategy is only as strong as its weakest link — every component from branding to structured interviewing must work in harmony to deliver better hiring results ." Strong recruitment systems depend on optimizing each core component: Employer branding – Attracts top talent organically; weak branding results in fewer qualified applicants. Talent pipeline development – Builds a ready pool of candidates; weak pipelines lead to slower time-to-hire. Structured interviewing – Ensures consistent candidate evaluation; poor structure creates biased or inconsistent decisions. Data-driven decision-making – Improves hiring outcomes; lack of data leads to missed opportunities for improvement. 💡 Tip: Treat your recruitment strategy as an ecosystem , not a checklist — every element must be actively maintained to keep the system performing at its peak. ⚠️ Warning: Neglecting even one pillar of your recruitment strategy can create a ripple effect that slows down the entire hiring process and costs your organization top-tier candidates . 1. Build a Strong Employer Brand Most candidates form opinions about your organization before recruiters contact them, based on reviews, LinkedIn, and employee testimonials. According to the iCIMS Blog , companies with strong employer brands see 50% more qualified applicants, so brand perception directly shapes the quality of the applicant pool. Employer branding requires consistent, specific content: real employee stories, honest descriptions of career progression, and authentic leadership voices. Authenticity filters for candidates who genuinely fit while repelling poor matches. 2. Develop Talent Pipelines Before Vacancies Open Most organizations begin recruiting when a job opening appears, starting from scratch, incurring higher costs and longer time-to-fill windows . Building talent pipelines before you need them transforms recruitment from a reactive scramble into a predictable, manageable process. Effective pipeline development means staying in contact with passive candidates through recruitment marketing, maintaining talent communities, and treating previous applicants as long-term assets. When a role opens, you reach out to people who already know your organization and have expressed interest. 3. Use Employee Referral Programs The best hires often come through people already inside the organization. CPS HR Consulting reports that employee referrals account for 30-40% of all hires at many organizations because employees understand the culture, pace, and expectations better than any job description can convey. A referral program only works if it's easy to use and consistently reinforced. Complicated submission processes, unclear reward structures , or poor communication after a referral will kill participation. The mechanics matter as much as the incentive. 4. Invest in Recruitment CRM and Candidate Relationship Management A recruitment CRM stores candidate profiles, tracks interactions, and organizes talent pools so recruiters can re-engage strong fits who weren't ready to move when first contacted. This builds talent acquisition over time rather than treating each hiring cycle as a fresh start. Spreadsheets and basic ATS notes create gaps as candidate volumes grow: follow-ups get missed, warm candidates go cold, and sourcing work repeats quarterly. Platforms like Cercli integrate recruitment, HR, and workforce management into a single platform, preventing candidate relationships from falling through the cracks between disconnected tools. 5. Combine AI With Human Decision-Making AI handles volume well: screening applications , flagging candidates who meet core criteria, summarising profiles, and scheduling interviews. This frees recruiters for work requiring human judgment—assessing cultural alignment, reading communication style, and evaluating whether someone's potential fits the team's direction. AI should reduce friction and improve consistency, not replace the professional instincts that make hiring decisions defensible. Organizations that use AI as a filter while keeping humans in the decision seat move faster without sacrificing quality. 6. Strengthen Your Careers Site and Application Experience A slow, unclear, or mobile-unfriendly careers site immediately loses qualified candidates. Your application experience reflects how your organization works: a clunky process suggests internal friction, while a clean, fast one suggests respect for candidates' time. Focus on specific improvements: clear job descriptions with realistic expectations, a mobile-optimized application form, and acknowledgment emails sent within minutes of submission each reduce drop-off at different stages. Measure candidate conversion rate as a metric, not an assumed outcome. 7. Expand Sourcing Across Multiple Channels Using only job boards reaches only active candidates already looking for work. Passive candidates, often the best performers, require different approaches: LinkedIn outreach, industry communities, university partnerships, and internal mobility programs. Evaluate channels by quality of hires , not application volume. A channel driving 40% of applications but only 5% of successful hires wastes budget. 8. Use Skills-Based Hiring Where Appropriate Many organizations are finding that degree requirements and linear career paths poorly measure actual ability. Skills-based hiring uses practical tests, technical exercises, and structured interviews to evaluate what candidates can do, rather than relying on credentials as shortcuts. This approach expands the talent pool and identifies candidates with transferable skills who would otherwise be filtered out early. The shift also reduces unconscious bias in screening. When evaluation criteria are based on demonstrated skills rather than background markers, hiring decisions become more consistent and defensible. 9. Improve Collaboration Between Recruiters and Hiring Managers Recruitment slows when recruiters and hiring managers operate from different understandings of job requirements. Before candidate searches begin, both groups must align on key skills, disqualifying factors, interview processes, and timelines. This alignment meeting prevents weeks of mismatched candidate lists and circular feedback. When both sides can see where candidates are in the process, everyone stays accountable for their part. Hiring managers can track candidate movement through each stage, recruiters can access feedback immediately, and decisions are made faster, with fewer good candidates lost to delays. 10. Prioritize Candidate Experience Throughout the Hiring Process Every touchpoint in your hiring process communicates something about your organization. A week of silence after an interview, a generic rejection email, or a scheduling process that requires five back-and-forth messages all leave impressions that candidates carry forward. Employer reputation is built one candidate interaction at a time. Even rejected candidates can become advocates or future applicants if the experience was respectful and clear. Acceptance rates, candidate satisfaction scores, and time-to-respond metrics reflect the quality of experience you're delivering, not process speed alone. 11. Measure Recruitment Performance With Meaningful Metrics Most recruitment reporting fails by focusing on volume metrics while ignoring quality indicators. Time to hire and cost per hire matter, but quality of hire, offer acceptance rate , and hiring manager satisfaction reveal whether the process produces business results. Regular reporting against these metrics identifies where the process breaks down. If qualified applicant rates are high but offer acceptance is low, the problem lies in later stages, not sourcing. Metrics make bottlenecks visible, enabling fixes. 12. Job markets change, candidate preferences shift, and new tools open up new possibilities. A hiring plan that worked well eighteen months ago might now be slower, more costly, or less effective. Building regular check-ins into your hiring operations keeps the plan current without requiring a complete overhaul. But knowing which strategies work is only part of the picture. Where data privacy becomes a hiring risk Protecting candidate data is one of the biggest compliance risks organizations miss in regional recruitment. Both the UAE and Saudi Arabia have passed Personal Data Protection Laws that control how personal information is collected, stored, and shared during the hiring process. Collecting more candidate information than the job requires, or working with third-party recruitment providers that do not comply with local privacy standards, creates a risk that most organizations discover only after a breach occurs. Answers to common questions about fiber optic systems
summary: Want to build a network that’s fast, reliable and future-proof? Start by mastering the basics of how fiber optic systems work. Read our blog.
body_text: Being familiar with how fiber optic systems work means getting back to the fundamentals so you can make smarter technology decisions. But I’ve noticed that questions about the basics come up often, no matter how experienced someone is. When I joined Belden a few years ago after working in the power distribution industry, I quickly realized that even seasoned professionals can benefit from clear, straightforward answers to foundational fiber questions. That’s why I put together these insights, based on presentations I often give to industry professionals to make it easier to understand what fiber really is. How are fiber optic systems different from copper? While copper cables transmit data using electrical signals, fiber uses light. By transmitting data as pulses of light rather than electrical currents, fiber optic cables eliminate many of the limitations associated with copper cables, such as excessive heat generation, concern about bundle sizes, signal degradation over distance and susceptibility to electromagnetic interference. These limitations can become issues in certain high-speed, high-density environments. But fiber is designed to overcome them. Because it transmits data as pulses of light (and at the speed of light), it can carry more information much faster and over longer distances. And because it’s immune to electromagnetic interference and uses glass instead of metal, it offers minimal signal loss. Signals remain strong and clear. One important consideration to note, however, is that fiber has its tradeoffs, just like any technology: It can’t transmit power like copper cables can. Today, it can only transmit data. How do fiber optic systems work? A fiber optic cable sends pulses of light (data) through thin strands of glass “fibers.” The heart of a fiber is its glass core, which sits in the middle of the cable, giving light a path to travel down the cable to a receiving device. Data travels quickly through the fiber by bouncing along the core. The core is surrounded by: Cladding, which is a layer of glass that surrounds the core and contains light pulses to prevent loss Coating, which prevents scratching and other physical damage Buffer, which provides more protection and makes the fiber easier to install Armoring, which protects against damage from crushing, bending and harsh environmental conditions These inner components are enclosed inside a jacket, which protects everything inside. The type of jacket determines which environments the cable can withstand. The cable’s construction allows the fiber to bend and rotate without snapping What’s the difference between singlemode and multimode fiber? Fiber optic cables are categorized into two groups: singlemode and multimode . Each features a different core size to support different transmission distances and bandwidths. Singlemode has a small core that allows a single path (mode) for light to travel through. It’s designed to transmit data across long distances (up to several miles) with little signal loss. These cables are usually yellow in color. Multimode has a larger core that allows multiple light paths (modes) to travel through the cable at the same time. It uses either LEDs or VCSELs (vertical-cavity surface-emitting lasers) as light sources. Multimode fiber is ideal for distances of up to a few hundred meters. These cables are usually aqua or erika violet in color. These cables can be joined in one of two ways: Mechanical splicing “holds” the fiber ends together with a special connector Fusion splicing “fuses” or “welds” the fiber ends together using an electric arc What’s the difference between fiber connectors? To connect fiber optic cables, there are several types of fiber connectors to choose from. LC (lucent connector or little connector) connectors are common today, especially in high-density environments like data centers. Because they’re small, cost-effective and easy to install, they are widely used. ST (straight tip) connectors are one of the oldest types of fiber connectors, often found in legacy installations. Made of metal, they’re not suitable for today’s high-density environments, but they are still being used in older systems. SC (subscriber connector or square connector) connectors are slightly larger than LC connectors but are still very popular due to their reliability. MPO (multi-fiber push-on) connectors are newer connectors made for high-density applications, connecting up to 12 fibers through a single plug. VSFF (very small form factor) connectors are ultra-compact connectors that allow for more connections in smaller spaces. How are fiber optic cabling systems managed? In copper systems, components like patch panels are used to organize, protect and manage connections. In fiber systems, connections are managed with cassettes and frames. Frames are centralized hubs that connect and route fiber cables. Connectors can be plugged into the front and back of a frame, and frame options range from simple adapter plates for basic connectivity to more advanced optical distribution frames (ODFs), which are entire cabinets built for high-capacity, high-density environments. Cassettes combine frames and splice trays, housing spliced fibers to maintain proper bend radius and protect connectors. They’re easy to patch in and out. Making the right fiber optic system connections While these questions might seem straightforward, they come up often when discussing fiber optic systems. Having a solid grasp of the basics will help ensure that your network connections are reliable and future-ready. Have questions about fiber optic systems that we didn’t cover in this list? Send us a note; we’ll be happy to answer them! Get answers to your fiber questions. title: Best AI Transcription Software: Top 6 Tools Tested in July 2026
summary: We tested AI transcription software in July 2026. Compare real-time transcription, speaker ID quality, and integration depth across 6 top platforms.
body_text: We tested 6 AI transcription tools in June 2026 because the category has split. Some tools transcribe and stop. Others extract decisions, file tickets, and close the loop before your standup ends. You’re comparing Otter AI sign up flows, best ai transcription software free reddit threads, free automatic transcription software downloads, audio transcription software installs, transcription software free download links for PC, best ai transcription free for PC and best ai transcription app for iphone picks. The real question isn’t transcription accuracy anymore (most tools clear 90% under clean conditions). It’s what happens after the transcript lands. Does it surface action items? Does it route them into Jira or Linear? Or does it hand you a 12-page document and leave the manual work on your plate? This breakdown covers transcription quality, speaker ID under real conditions, integration depth, free tiers that actually work. TLDR: AI transcription tools convert audio to text, but the gap between transcript and action matters most Tools ranked on accuracy across noisy conditions, speaker ID quality, and integration depth with Jira/Slack Otter offers 300 free minutes monthly but stops at transcripts with no ticket creation Spinach files Jira tickets with owners during the call, closing the loop before the meeting ends Spinach fits engineering teams running 4+ weekly ceremonies where manual re-entry accumulates fast What Is AI Transcription Software? AI transcription software uses speech recognition and AI models to automatically convert spoken audio into written text. Feed it a recording, or let it join a live call, and it produces a transcript in seconds without requiring someone to type out every word by hand. The category has grown well beyond raw transcription. Early tools produced walls of text and called it done. Newer tools extract decisions, surface action items, assign owners, and generate summaries from the same audio. AI transcription accuracy benchmark on clean audio, per AssemblyAI’s benchmark, but the gap between “here’s what was said” and “here’s what happens next” is where the most meaningful differentiation between tools actually lives, especially when only 39% of employees receive post-meeting action items despite 54% wanting them, according to Zoom’s meeting statistics research . How We Ranked AI Transcription Software Assessing AI transcription tools requires more than running a few test recordings. Each tool below was assessed against a consistent set of criteria so the rankings reflect real-world performance instead of feature marketing. Here is what drove the scores: Transcription accuracy across audio conditions, including noisy environments, heavy accents, and multi-speaker calls where voices overlap Real-time vs. async processing, since live transcription and file-upload workflows serve fundamentally different use cases Speaker identification quality, because a transcript that labels every line as “Speaker 1” adds manual cleanup time Integration depth with tools like Zoom, Google Meet, Slack, and Jira Free tier and trial availability, since access without a credit card matters for teams testing before committing Pricing transparency across tiers, including where caps and paywalls kick in Best Overall AI Transcription Software: Spinach AI Spinach AI sits at the top of this list not because it transcribes meetings, but because it closes the loop that every other tool on this list leaves open. Transcription is the input. Decisions, action items, and filed tickets are the output. Spinach joins your Zoom, Google Meet, or Microsoft Teams call in real time, captures what gets decided, and surfaces assigned action items before the call ends. A Scrum Master running four ceremonies a week stops spending 10 to 15 minutes after each one re-keying notes into Jira or Linear. That overhead disappears during the meeting, not after the transcript lands. Where tools like Otter or Fireflies hand you a text file and stop, Spinach routes outputs directly into your project management stack. Jira, Linear, Asana, ClickUp, and Notion are all supported. The ticket gets filed with context, an owner, and a due date, far beyond a quote pulled from a transcript. What Spinach Does That Transcription Tools Skip Most AI transcription tools are accurate at capturing words. Spinach is accurate at capturing what those words mean for your sprint. Real-time meeting facilitation: Spinach runs agenda items, tracks time, and flags blockers during the meeting, not after someone reads a transcript. Automatic ticket creation: Action items from standups, planning sessions, and retros become Jira or Linear tickets with owners assigned, filed before the call ends. Decision capture: Spinach logs what was decided instead of what was said, so there is a searchable record of outcomes without the 40-minute wall of text. Native integrations: Slack, Jira, Linear, Asana, ClickUp, Notion, Google Calendar, and Outlook are all supported without middleware. Who Should Use Spinach Engineering leads and Scrum Masters running daily standups, sprint planning, and retros with five or more attendees get the most out of Spinach. The real-time ticket-filing removes the manual re-entry that accumulates across every ceremony. Solo users uploading the occasional recording will find the outcomes layer less relevant than teams with a recurring Agile cadence. Otter Otter is one of the most recognized names in AI transcription, with over 25 million users. It offers real-time transcription, speaker identification, and meeting summaries across Zoom, Google Meet, and Microsoft Teams. The free tier gives you 300 transcription minutes per month, which covers occasional use but hits limits fast for daily standups or back-to-back interviews. Paid plans start at $16.99/month and add features like custom vocabulary and longer recording limits. Where Otter stops: it delivers a transcript. There are no action items filed, no tickets created, no outcomes tracked. For students capturing lectures or individuals transcribing interviews, that’s enough. For agile teams running ceremonies daily, the transcript is just the beginning of the work. Fireflies.ai Fireflies.ai is a solid choice for teams that need quick, searchable transcripts without much setup. It records meetings across Zoom, Google Meet, and Teams, then produces a transcript with speaker labels, a summary, and a searchable archive your whole team can access. Where it stops short is the handoff. Fireflies gives you the record of what was said, but filing tickets, assigning owners, and updating your backlog still falls on you. For engineering teams running four or five ceremonies a week, that manual step accumulates fast. Who should use Fireflies Teams that primarily need a searchable conversation archive and don’t require real-time ticket creation. If your workflow already has a dedicated person handling post-meeting task triage, Fireflies fits cleanly. If your Scrum Master is also expected to run retros, manage the backlog, and close the loop on action items before the next standup , the gap becomes friction every single day. Fathom Fathom records, transcribes, and summarizes video calls with a focus on keeping the experience lightweight and free. Its free tier is genuinely generous, covering unlimited recordings and transcripts for individuals, which makes it a frequent recommendation in “best free transcription” threads on Reddit. Where Fathom stops: the output is a meeting summary and transcript. There is no ticket creation, no sprint context, and no path from “action item discussed” to “task filed in Jira.” For a solo user capturing client calls or interviews, that is fine. For an engineering team running standups and planning sessions, the gap between transcript and ticket is where time gets lost. Fathom fits teams that want clean, free call recordings with readable summaries. It does not fit teams that need the meeting to produce work; a record alone won’t close the loop. Tactiq Tactiq records and transcribes meetings directly in your browser, requiring no desktop app download. It works as a Chrome extension for Google Meet, Zoom, and Microsoft Teams, making it one of the lower-friction setups in this roundup. What Tactiq Does Well Real-time captions appear during the meeting, so you can follow along even with noisy audio or accented speakers. Transcripts are timestamped and speaker-labeled, and you can mark key moments mid-call for faster review afterward. The free tier includes unlimited transcriptions, which stands out compared to tools that cap free usage at a few hours per month. Where Tactiq Stops Short Tactiq generates summaries and lets you extract action items post-meeting, but the output is manual. You get a transcript and a text block; what happens next is on you. There is no native ticket creation, no Jira or Linear integration, and no real-time decision capture that feeds directly into your workflow. For a solo researcher or student capturing interview notes, that workflow is fine. For an engineering team running four ceremonies a week, re-keying action items from a text summary into Jira after every call adds up fast. Spinach joins the same meetings and closes that loop before the call ends, turning decisions into assigned tickets without the manual handoff. Jamie Jamie is an AI meeting assistant built for individual contributors instead of teams, with a strong focus on private, local-first note-taking. Unlike most transcription tools that process audio on remote servers, Jamie runs processing on-device by default, which appeals to users with strict data privacy requirements. title: Airbnb.org provides free emergency housing after Texas floods
summary: To support communities affected by flooding in Central and South Texas, Airbnb.org, a nonprofit founded by Airbnb to provide emergency housing in times of crisis, is working with nonprofit partners to offer free emergency housing to displaced residents and first responders.
body_text: To support communities affected by flooding in Central and South Texas, Airbnb.org , a nonprofit founded by Airbnb to provide emergency housing in times of crisis, is working with nonprofit partners to offer free emergency housing to displaced residents and first responders. Airbnb.org is partnering with Catholic Charities, Archdiocese of San Antonio to connect displaced residents with free temporary housing. Meanwhile, Airbnb.org is also working with All Hands & Hearts and Operation Blessing to provide housing for their first responders supporting relief efforts. “A comfortable place to call home can help people recover after a disaster, while providing first responders an opportunity to unwind and recharge for the next day,” said Christoph Gorder, Executive Director of Airbnb.org. “We were there for Texas after last summer’s tragic flooding. Working with many of the same partners, including Catholic Charities and All Hands & Hearts, we’re committed to helping the region recover from this latest round of severe weather.” “Our hearts go out to everyone affected by this devastating flooding. We are committed to providing immediate and ongoing support to help our communities recover,” said Ada Saenz, CEO/President of Catholic Charities, Archdiocese of San Antonio. “But we cannot do this alone. The generosity and involvement of our community members play a crucial role in our relief efforts. Every donation makes a meaningful difference in helping families rebuild their lives.” “All Hands & Hearts is proud to stand alongside Airbnb.org in supporting communities affected by the Texas floods,” said Alix Seyfarth, Director of Strategy, All Hands & Hearts. “Right now, our teams are on the ground in Kerr County, and Airbnb’s emergency housing support is providing displaced families and responders a safe place to stay as recovery efforts continue. This partnership reflects the kind of coordinated, community-first response disaster survivors need.” “We’re deeply grateful to Airbnb.org for partnering with Operation Blessing as we respond to disasters, including in Texas. By providing housing for our disaster relief teams, Airbnb.org enables us to focus on what matters most—serving families as they begin the long road to recovery,” said Drew Friedrich, President of Operation Blessing. How it works Airbnb.org partners with local organizations before disaster strikes, so housing support is available quickly. Catholic Charities, Archdiocese of San Antonio is identifying residents in need of temporary housing and referring them to Airbnb.org, which provides credits to book a nearby Airbnb stay that meets their needs—often close to their workplaces, schools, or support networks. Stays are free for guests and are funded by Airbnb.org and the generosity of donors. Residents impacted by flooding in Central and South Texas can request temporary housing support by contacting Catholic Charities, Archdiocese of San Antonio: Region 1 – Texas Hill Country: 210-718-5837 . Counties: Kerr, Kendall, Bandera, Real, Edwards Region 2 – Highway 90 Corridor: 210-935-5885 . Counties: Medina, Uvalde, Frio Region 3 – San Antonio Area: 210-305-6010 . Counties: Bexar, Comal, Atascosa, Wilson, Guadalupe, Gonzales, Karnes Region 4 – Del Rio and Brackettville: 210-278-8381 . Counties: Val Verde, Edwards, Kinney How to help Anyone interested in supporting those impacted by the flooding in Central and South Texas can help by donating to Airbnb.org. 100 percent of donations go directly toward connecting people in crisis with emergency housing. So far this year, Airbnb.org has provided nearly 7,000 nights of free emergency housing in Texas, including after the wildfires in the Texas Panhandle this spring.

title: What Do We Know About Who Watches Major League Baseball on TV and Streaming?
summary: 162 games. Nightly reach. Fans with real spending power. Here's what the viewership data says about who watches MLB on TV and streaming.
body_text: Major League Baseball is massive. Everybody knows it, and the numbers prove it. The 2024 World Series drew an average of 15.81 million viewers across platforms, the most-watched Fall Classic since 2017. The 2025 regular season posted year-over-year viewership gains across every national broadcast partner. MLB.TV recorded 14.5 billion minutes watched in 2024 , then topped it again in 2025 with streaming numbers up 34% from the prior year . Scale is not a question here. But scale is just the opening pitch. The more interesting part of the MLB audience story is about who’s doing the watching now, and the answer has shifted more in the last three years than it did in the previous fifteen. The Audience Everyone Already Suspects Is There MLB’s core viewership is broad, loyal, and heavily invested. The sport draws the second-largest total audience of any professional league in the U.S., trailing only the NFL, and its 162-game regular season means that presence isn’t seasonal, but a nightly drumbeat from April through October. A January 2024 SBRnet survey found that the largest single age segment among MLB attendees and viewers was 50-64, which tracks with a generation that grew up watching games as a social ritual, passed it down, and never really stopped. For advertisers, the profile that follows — established careers, dual-income households, strong brand loyalty, discretionary spending on entertainment and lifestyle — is straightforwardly valuable. According to The Shelf’s analysis of professional sports fan demographics , MLB fans across the five major leagues are consistently described as middle-class men and women with meaningful disposable income across multiple spending categories. The Part of the Audience That Surprises Most Marketers Here’s where the conventional wisdom starts getting complicated. For years, MLB carried a reputation as a sport with an aging problem. The average age of a fan was trending up, and younger audiences seemed to be drifting away. That reputation is starting to change, thanks in part to the pitch clock era, which began in 2023, and compressed games to under two hours and forty minutes on average, the shortest since the mid-1980s. Shorter games increase accessibility, and when combined with a new generation of genuinely marketable stars, younger audiences have become more inclined to take themselves out to the ballgame from the comfort of their own couch. According to MLB , the median age of a ticket buyer has dropped from 51 to 45 since 2019 — a six-year shift in under five years. On the streaming side, the movement is clearer still: the average age of an MLB.TV subscriber dropped from 48 to 44 over the same period. Viewership in the 18-34 demographic grew 12% on ESPN, 24% on FS1, and 9% on Fox during the 2024 season. The network-level growth in this demo was broad enough that Barrett Media noted a 13% gain in 18-34 viewers for the MLB Network Showcase Game series alone in 2025. What’s driving younger fans toward streaming specifically? Partly platform access — younger fans, particularly those aged 18-34, are more than twice as likely to stream live sports compared to older demographics, according to Viant Technology. And MLB has deliberately expanded its streaming footprint to meet them there. As of 2025, 26 of the league’s 30 teams offer standalone DTC streaming options for local fans. The infrastructure is there; the audience is showing up. For advertisers, the 18-34 streaming fan is worth separating from the broader “MLB audience” label. This viewer is paying for access, often out-of-market, actively following a specific team across a long season. That level of intent signals a different kind of attention than someone who happens to catch a game occasionally on cable. The Audience Most Brands Are Underestimating According to ACR viewership data from LG Ad Solutions , female viewership of MLB has seen consistent growth. Because of the stereotype that typical sports fans are male, that finding tends to catch people off-guard, but it aligns with something The Shelf’s analysis found: baseball fans are often described as the most family-oriented fan group among the five major American professional sports leagues. The family dimension of MLB viewership changes how advertisers should think about the audience. A game that runs two and a half hours on a weeknight, in a sport with nearly daily games over six months, tends to pull households into shared viewing in ways that shorter or less frequent sports don’t. It’s background viewing that becomes active viewing when someone hits a grand slam. It’s also a format that holds up across generations in the same room, where a grandparent, a parent, and a teenager can all plausibly have an opinion on who is at-bat. Fifty-seven percent of MLB fans report that they like to stream live sports , according to LG Ad Solutions’ 2022 ACR data, a figure that tracks with the broader directional shift toward streaming across all live sports. That distribution matters: an MLB audience that spans broadcast, CTV, and mobile isn’t consolidated in one place, which means brands that show up across platforms have a better shot at reaching the full household than those anchored to a single linear buy. The female viewer and the co-viewing household don’t always show up in the top-line MLB audience conversation. They should. Both represent reach beyond the assumed sports-fan demographic, and both are watching games in the same high-attention context as the core audience. What This Means for Advertisers Major League Baseball offers a live sports placement without the congestion of the NFL window, across a season that runs nightly from April through the World Series. The audience story above points to a mix of loyal older viewers, a younger streaming cohort that’s actively growing, and a household audience with more breadth than the conventional male sports demo would suggest. For brands in categories like financial services, auto, consumer electronics, retail, food and beverage, or travel, the sustained attention and multi-demographic reach of a full-season MLB buy creates the kind of repeat exposure that builds familiarity, recall, and consideration over time, not just around one event in October.

title: SRE On-Call Strategy: Best Practices for Scaling Reliability
summary: Cut triage time by 80% with Struct's SRE on-call best practices — SLO alerting, blameless postmortems, and AI-assisted remediation. Book a demo today.
body_text: SRE On-Call Strategy: Best Practices for Scaling Reliability July 11, 2026 Written by: Nimesh Chakravarthi, Co-founder & CTO, Struct Key Takeaways Healthy on-call programs target no more than 2 actionable pages per engineer per shift, a false-positive rate below 10%, and MTTR under 15 minutes. A seven-step playbook starts with a baseline audit of pages, false positives, MTTR, and runbook coverage before any changes happen. Core practices include SLO-based alerting, a “no runbook, no page” policy, AI-assisted first-pass investigation, equitable rotations, blameless postmortems, a pager health dashboard, and quarterly maturity reviews. Teams move through four maturity stages, from manual triage to full AI-assisted remediation, while keeping existing tools and workflows. Struct helps teams reduce triage time by 80%, compressing a 45-minute manual investigation to under 5 minutes for Seed to Series C companies. See how Struct compresses triage time and get your first AI-generated investigation running in under 10 minutes. Section 1 – Define the Objective and Current State Start by auditing four baseline numbers: pages per shift, false-positive percentage, MTTR, and runbook coverage. Use the checklist below to capture your current state in a single sitting. Metric How to Measure Healthy Target Owner Pages per shift PagerDuty or alerting tool export, 30-day rolling ≤2 actionable On-call lead False-positive rate (Non-actionable pages ÷ total pages) × 100 <10% On-call lead MTTR Incident tool: time-to-acknowledge to time-to-resolve <15 min Engineering manager Runbook coverage Count alerts with linked runbooks ÷ total alerts 100% SRE team Any metric outside its target becomes a prioritized input to the seven steps below. These steps address the root causes behind poor on-call metrics. Steps 1 and 2 reduce false positives and MTTR by improving alert quality. Step 3 accelerates triage through automation. Steps 4 and 5 prevent burnout and capture systemic improvements. Steps 6 and 7 ensure the gains persist over time. Section 2 – 7-Step On-Call Scaling Playbook 1. Set SLO-Based, Actionable-Only Alerting Rules The goal is to page engineers only when an SLO burn rate threatens an error budget within a defined window. The SRE lead owns this work and starts from defined SLOs per service and historical error-rate data. From those inputs, the team creates alert rules tied to multi-window burn-rate thresholds, such as paging when 2% of the error budget is consumed in 1 hour. This approach requires upfront SLO definition, so teams without SLOs must define them first or use a proxy metric such as 5xx rate above a rolling baseline. 2. Enforce a “No Runbook, No Page” Alert Policy The goal is to eliminate alerts that fire without a documented response path. The engineering manager and alert author share ownership and begin with an alert inventory and the existing runbook repository. They then add a gate in CI or CD that blocks alert deployment if no runbook URL is attached. This policy slows initial alert creation, and that friction is intentional because it reduces noise and confusion later. 3. Automate First-Pass Investigation with AI Tooling The goal is to deliver a correlated root-cause summary before the on-call engineer opens their laptop. The SRE lead and tooling owner manage this step using the alert channel, observability integrations, and runbook instructions as inputs. The AI layer produces an auto-generated timeline, blast-radius summary, and suggested fix within 5 minutes of the alert firing. This approach depends on clean telemetry, so teams with sparse logging will see lower accuracy. The 80% triage-time reduction mentioned earlier translates to compressing a 45-minute manual investigation into under 5 minutes for Seed to Series C companies. Get your first AI investigation running and see this workflow in your own alert channel. 4. Design Fair Rotations and Clear Compensation The goal is to distribute on-call load fairly and compensate engineers for after-hours work. The engineering manager owns this step and uses team size, time zones, and pages-per-shift data to design the schedule. The output is a rotation with at least 5 engineers per pool, a clear compensation policy using cash, comp time, or both, and a shadow rotation that helps onboard junior engineers. Smaller teams with fewer than 5 engineers face unavoidable concentration risk, so they should first reduce alert volume. 5. Run Blameless Post-Incident Reviews with Owners The goal is to turn every significant incident into a systemic improvement with a named owner and due date. The incident commander and engineering manager lead this work using the incident timeline, contributing factors, and action items as inputs. They publish a written postmortem within 48 hours, track action items in the team’s ticketing system, and schedule a 30-day follow-up review. This process requires protected calendar time, or action items stall and the practice loses credibility. 6. Create a Shared Pager Health Dashboard Track the six KPIs below on a shared dashboard that the engineering manager and on-call lead review monthly. This view keeps the team aligned on pager load, quality, and follow-through. KPI Definition Target Review Cadence Pages per shift Actionable pages per engineer per 8-hour shift ≤2 Monthly False-positive rate Non-actionable pages ÷ total pages <10% Monthly MTTR Acknowledge to resolve, median <15 min Monthly Runbook coverage Alerts with linked runbooks ÷ total alerts 100% Monthly Postmortem completion rate Postmortems published within 48 h ÷ P1/P2 incidents 100% Monthly Action-item closure rate Postmortem action items closed on time ÷ total ≥80% Quarterly 7. Hold a Quarterly On-Call Maturity Review The goal is to prevent metric drift and move the team along the maturity roadmap. The engineering manager and SRE lead own this review and use the pager health dashboard, postmortem backlog, and error-budget reports as inputs. They leave the session with updated alert rules, rotation adjustments, and a prioritized improvement list for the next quarter. Quarterly reviews form the minimum effective cadence, while monthly reviews work better during rapid growth. Section 3 – How This Playbook Fits Daily Engineering Work The seven steps above map directly onto tools engineering teams already use. Alerts originate in observability platforms and route into the team’s communication hub and incident-management system. Runbooks live in the source-control repository alongside the services they describe, which keeps them versioned with the code. Post-incident action items land in the existing ticketing system so they compete for sprint capacity alongside feature work. Workflow Stage Tool Category Integration Point Output Alert fire Observability platform Webhook to incident channel Structured alert payload First-pass investigation AI triage layer Reads logs, traces, code, posts summary Root-cause report in channel Escalation & coordination Incident management Auto-creates incident record Timeline, responder assignment Resolution & follow-up Ticketing + source control Action items linked to postmortem PR or task with owner and due date No new communication channels are required. The AI triage layer operates inside the existing alert thread, so engineers receive context without switching tools. Once this workflow lives inside current tools, the next step is to measure whether it actually improves on-call health. Section 4 – Measurement and Continuous Improvement The six KPIs from the pager health dashboard drive two review loops. A monthly dashboard review catches metric drift early, and a quarterly roadmap update advances the maturity stage. Engineering managers own the monthly review. The quarterly update requires sign-off from the VP of Engineering or equivalent so improvement work receives sprint allocation. Start capturing triage-time data from day one and give your pager health dashboard a reliable baseline. Section 5 – Common Pitfalls and Practical Fixes Pitfall Symptom Mitigation Alert overload False-positive rate >30%, engineers silence alerts Enforce SLO-based burn-rate thresholds, delete alerts with no action in 90 days Missing runbooks MTTR spikes on unfamiliar services CI gate blocks alert deployment without runbook URL Tribal knowledge concentration Junior engineers escalate every page to one senior AI first-pass investigation provides context, shadow rotations transfer knowledge Weak escalation paths Incidents stall when primary responder is unavailable Define and test secondary and tertiary escalation paths in the rotation tool Engineer burnout Voluntary attrition spikes, sick days cluster after on-call weeks Cap pages per shift at ≤2, compensate explicitly, keep rotation pool size at 5 or more 2026 On-Call Maturity Roadmap Stage Description Target Metrics Key Enabler Stage 0 – Manual Triage Engineers hunt logs across tools with no runbooks MTTR >45 min, false positives >40% Baseline audit (Section 1) Stage 1 – Structured Response SLO-based alerts, full runbook coverage, blameless postmortems running MTTR <30 min, false positives <20% Steps 1–2 and 5 Stage 2 – AI-Assisted Triage Automated first-pass investigation, pager health dashboard live MTTR <15 min, false positives <10%, triage time −80% Steps 3 and 6, AI investigation layer Stage 3 – Full AI-Assisted Remediation AI suggests and drafts fixes, error-budget policy gates releases, chaos engineering validates resilience MTTR <10 min, pages per shift ≤1, junior engineers self-sufficient Steps 4 and 7, code-agent handoff Frequently Asked Questions What is the minimum team size or tooling maturity needed to start this playbook? Teams as small as three to five engineers can implement Steps 1, 2, and 5 immediately using any standard alerting and incident-management tool. AI-assisted triage in Step 3 requires existing observability instrumentation, at minimum structured logs with trace IDs and an alert channel in Slack or a ticketing system. Teams without basic logging should instrument services first, because the accuracy of automated investigation depends directly on telemetry quality. How much engineering time does integration actually take? Connecting an AI investigation layer to an existing Slack alerting channel, a code repository, and an observability platform takes under 10 minutes for teams already using those tools. The setup time mentioned earlier, under 10 minutes, applies to teams that already rely on Slack, a code repository, and an observability platform. The first automated investigation runs immediately after connection and provides a working baseline for the pager health dashboard from day one. What happens if our logging and telemetry are poor quality? AI-assisted triage relies on the data available in connected systems. Sparse logs, missing trace IDs, or unstructured log formats reduce the accuracy of automated root-cause analysis. The practical mitigation is to treat telemetry quality as a prerequisite. Add structured logging and trace propagation to the highest-traffic services first, then expand AI triage coverage as instrumentation improves. Teams with poor telemetry still benefit from Steps 1, 2, 4, and 5, which do not depend on AI tooling. How do junior engineers safely take on-call shifts without deep system knowledge? Two mechanisms make junior on-call safe. A shadow rotation pairs juniors with a senior for two to four weeks before independent shifts and uses real incidents as training material. AI first-pass investigation then provides a contextualized starting point, including blast radius, correlated timeline, and suggested fix, for every alert. Juniors can follow the AI-generated summary and escalate only when the suggested path does not resolve the issue, instead of escalating by default. Is an AI investigation tool compliant with strict security and data requirements? Struct is SOC 2 and HIPAA compliant, which covers the compliance requirements of most Series A–C companies in the United States. Logs and telemetry data are accessed and processed ephemerally, and they are not stored beyond the investigation window. Teams with enterprise policies that require full on-premise deployment or zero-egress log access should confirm that a cloud-integrated tool fits their security posture before adoption. Conclusion Scaling on-call reliability without adding headcount requires a clean baseline audit, SLO-based alerting that removes noise at the source, AI-assisted first-pass investigation that compresses triage from 45 minutes to under 5, and a quarterly review cadence that prevents metric drift. The seven steps above provide a concrete, owner-assigned path from Stage 0 manual triage to Stage 3 AI-assisted remediation. The next frontier beyond this playbook couples the maturity roadmap with a formal error-budget policy that gates feature releases on reliability targets and validates resilience assumptions through structured chaos engineering experiments. Connect your integrations in under 10 minutes and let AI handle the next investigation before your engineer opens their laptop. Automate your on-call runbook Try It Today

title: Marcus & Millichap’s IPA Capital Markets Bolsters Its Eastern Region Capital Markets Team

In his new role, Demadis will report to Marc Sznajderman, senior managing director and head of production for the firm’s Eastern region. Demadis holds a Bachelor of Science degree in real estate and urban economics with a concentration in finance from the University of Connecticut School of Business. title: Carrier Wins the 2024 IoT Breakthrough of the Year Award for its Abound Edge System
summary: The Abound Edge System helps customers enhance the efficiency of their building operations.
body_text: PALM BEACH GARDENS, Fla., July 2, 2025 — Carrier Global Corporation (NYSE: CARR), is proud to announce that Carrier Abound has won IoThinkTank’s 2024 IoT Breakthrough of the Year Award for its Abound Edge system. This recognition highlights Carrier’s commitment to transforming the Internet of Things (IoT) landscape, particularly in optimizing building operations through connectivity, centralized management and artificial intelligence (AI) IoThinkTank, a leading platform dedicated to celebrating excellence in the IoT industry, recognizes companies, products, and individuals making significant strides in innovation and technological advancement. Their Best of 2024 Awards recognize groundbreaking achievements, visionary leadership and transformative solutions shaping the future of the Internet of Things. The Abound Edge System stood out for its ability to address a common challenge faced by business owners: the lack of visibility into how their buildings are performing due to insufficient automation and centralized intelligence. Carrier Abound tackles this challenge with a suite of digital solutions and services specifically designed for customers from a variety of industries. Using a combination of edge hardware, AI-powered software, and expert consulting services, the Abound Edge System transforms buildings into a fully connected ecosystem where AI can be applied and autonomous actions can be initiated, delivering enhanced occupant comfort, improved energy efficiency, and reduced operational costs across a building portfolio. The system aggregates, secures, transforms and optimizes data from connected edge devices, allowing for seamless communication using IoT technologies. It also supports automatic updates for the system itself and to connected devices. Features such as cloud-deployable program profile templates, centralized schedule and set-point management, and control logic configuration enable customers to effectively manage their buildings. Customers from diverse industries are already realizing significant savings with Carrier Abound. With management extending to over 33,000 sites, Carrier Abound has enabled multi-site clients to save over 6.5 billion kWh in energy use to date. In one instance, Carrier Abound helped a multi-site customer save over 10% in energy costs over a 3-year period.1 “We are thrilled to receive the IoThinkTank’s 2024 IoT Breakthrough of the Year Award”, said Yasir Qureshi, General Manager, Carrier Abound. “This achievement underscores our commitment to developing innovative solutions that deliver significant financial benefits for customers. As a leader in AI technology for buildings, we will continue our innovation journey and look forward to achieving even more impactful customer outcomes." For more information about Carrier Abound and how it can transform your building operations, please visit www.abound.carrier.com . 1 The customer used the Abound Edge system along with our managed services offering. About Carrier Carrier Global Corporation, global leader in intelligent climate and energy solutions, is committed to creating innovations that bring comfort, safety and sustainability to life. Through cutting-edge advancements in climate solutions such as temperature control, air quality and transportation, we improve lives, empower critical industries and ensure the safe transport of food, life-saving medicines and more. Since inventing modern air conditioning in 1902, we lead with purpose: enhancing the lives we live and the world we share. We continue to lead because of our world-class, inclusive workforce that puts the customer at the center of everything we do. For more information, visit corporate.carrier.com or follow Carrier on social media @Carrier . Carrier. For the World We Share.

title: Low-Touch Products
body_text: We don't want our users in our app every single day I’ve been thinking a lot about when it makes sense for a product to be low or high-touch, especially as it relates to how we build our product at Velos. There’s a temptation to want “usage”—users on your app for multiple hours a day. In our case, however, we really don’t want our users spending more than a few minutes on the platform every day. The best automation service is invisible, or at least operates in the background. The real interaction we care about is when the customer interacts with the outputs of our platform (or rather doesn’t raise any issue with them). There’re exceptions, but automation tools, like Velos, should help people automate manual tasks without requiring extensive time in a new app configuring, monitoring, and updating automations. An app that needs constant human input defeats the whole purpose of “automation”. Our customers don’t want to buy another tool that’s going to give them more work.

title: 5 Proven Growth Hacks to Skyrocket Your App’s Downloads and Revenue
summary: Unlock these effective strategies for app growth, from apps-gone-free campaigns to App Store features — all backed by real-world success examples.
body_text: In today's competitive market, standing out and driving downloads is more challenging than ever. But, it's also never been more important. Whether you're launching a new game, a productivity tool, or an innovative service, you need some strategies in place to break through the noise. Drawing from years of experience studying the app space while heading up App Masters and Indie App Santa, here are five of the most effective growth hacking strategies that I've seen. 1. Rethinking the apps gone free campaign One of the classic growth hacking techniques is the apps-gone-free campaign. Traditionally, this involves temporarily converting a paid app to free status for a limited period to create a surge of downloads. In today's landscape, this approach can be tweaked for modern monetization models. Instead of switching a paid app completely free, you can strategically offer a non-consumable in-app purchase (IAP) for free for a couple of days. Typically, the remove ads IAP works well for games whereas the lifetime IAP works better for subscription-based apps. By making a premium feature available at no cost for a limited time, you create urgency among potential users. The free offer acts as a powerful incentive — people who might hesitate to pay for premium features are now more willing to at least try the app. With increased downloads during this "promotional" period, many developers have seen not only a boost in user numbers, but also a significant increase in subsequent in-app purchases. Making more sales during an apps-gone-free campaign than in several months of standard operation. — An App Masters client For example, one client we tried this with even reported the above. Not bad! Success with this strategy also hinges on promotion. It's not enough to simply flip the pricing switch. There's simply too much out there now. So, get the word out and make that your priority. Leading technology sites like AppAdvice and Indie App Santa are ideal for this type of promotion, as well as relevant communities on Reddit (for example, the iOS apps subreddit). Remember, when offering an in-app purchase for free, ensure that it's non-consumable (think "Remove Ads" or "Unlock Premium Feature") so you preserve the value proposition and secure a lasting conversion once users experience the upgrade. 2. Mastering App Store Optimization (ASO) App Store Optimization, or ASO, is often referred to as SEO for the App Store, and it plays a crucial role in organic discovery. At its core, ASO is about ensuring your app stands out in a crowded marketplace by optimizing key elements of your app's store listing. This includes your app title, description, keywords, and even the icon and screenshots. It's a constantly evolving art, but it pays dividends once it's implemented correctly. Many critics argue that ASO isn't as effective as it once was. In truth, ASO continues to work — but only when your app delivers genuine value. ASO for a bad app won't matter. A great app with no ASO may not hit. You want both — an app genuinely solving a problem paired with effective ASO can equal an attractive business. Big brands, such as Uber or Kindle, have large marketing budgets and strong brand recognition that allow them to leverage ASO successfully. These companies invest in high-quality content and consistently update their listings to resonate with potential users. For smaller developers, though, the lesson is the same: a good ASO strategy can boost your organic downloads, but again — it requires an app that meets or exceeds user expectations. While ASO can be a massive topic to dive into, simply focus on the fundamentals first. Ensure your app's title is both catchy and descriptive, use a set of well-researched keywords, and back it all up with a strong user experience. In the past, I've even experimented with techniques like leveraging app store reviews to ramp up specific keyword rankings. I've found that strategy to be effective, and it continues to deliver results even today. The bottom line is that when executed correctly, ASO lays a solid foundation for your app's long-term visibility and success. Don't skip it! 3. Embracing localization for global reach Localization goes far beyond simply translating your app's language. It's about tailoring your app's entire presentation to speak directly to users in different regions. By localizing your app name, keywords, and (if possible) screenshots and descriptions, you can tap into markets that might be overlooked when you limit your content to English. Start small here, as with ASO. Try focusing on the most visible elements — things like your app's name and the keywords associated with it. For instance, subtle differences such as using "localised" instead of "localized" can make a significant impact in certain markets like the UK. Once you see an uptick in regional downloads, consider gradually localizing additional assets like screenshots and in-app descriptions. This incremental approach helps manage costs while measuring impact, ensuring that each step in localization is justified by increased user engagement. One minor downside of partial localization is that users in non-English speaking markets might find the in-app content still in English. However, the benefits of reaching a larger audience typically outweigh that. By adjusting your app's metadata for different regions, you offer a more personalized experience that can dramatically boost downloads in countries that would have otherwise been difficult to crack. 4. Leveraging exclusive PR opportunities Public relations still holds significant power in the digital age, especially when it comes to launching an app. Instead of spreading your story to multiple outlets, consider granting an exclusive to a single, respected publication. Pitching your launch as an exclusive story can help you secure quality coverage from top-tier media outlets like TechCrunch or VentureBeat, where it might be otherwise harder to gain attention. Here's how it works: Identify the right reporter or editor within the target publication. Tailor a pitch that not only explains your app's unique value, but also offers them the first look at your launch. Offer them exclusive rights to your story. Now, you're effectively flattering their credibility — and many publications appreciate that. This approach creates a sense of urgency and pride, which can lead to some favorable coverage. That said, there is a trade-off, though. By pitching an exclusive, you're limiting your audience to that one publication for the time being. If the pitch doesn't land, you may not have immediate alternatives. In one case, I pitched an exclusive to a well-known outlet only to receive a delayed response stating that the story had already been published elsewhere. Despite this small risk, the rewards are worth it when the exclusive generates buzz and positions your app as a must-watch launch. The key is to get in front of the media early in your launch cycle, securing the attention you need before your app goes live. 5. Cracking the App Store feature hack Finally, one of the most enticing strategies for app developers is the App Store feature hack. Securing a spot on the featured section in the App Store can lead to a massive influx of downloads. But, how do you get your app noticed by the right people at Apple? It starts with doing your homework. Every category in the App Store is carefully managed by a dedicated team. Use LinkedIn to identify the right App Store manager for your app's category and tools like Email Hunter to locate their email address quickly. Then, craft a compelling pitch explaining why your app deserves a feature placement. Timing is crucial here. Rather than pitching before your app is approved, wait until it has successfully passed review. This extra layer of credibility enhances your pitch and increases your chances of receiving a favorable response. You can even do this right within App Store Connect now (look at the sidebar under "Featuring" → "Nominations"). When reaching out, give them plenty of notice — ideally at least two to three weeks before your launch date. For certain categories, like gaming, there might even be a preference for specific launch days (one manager noted that Thursday is often ideal). While this method might take extra effort, landing a featured spot can exponentially increase your app's visibility, driving both organic downloads and long-term engagement. Wrapping up Growing an app successfully requires a multi-faceted approach rather than a single formula. All of these strategies play a crucial role in increasing downloads and engagement. To recap: A well-executed apps-gone-free campaign can drive an immediate surge in users. ASO ensures long-term visibility. Localization helps tap into new markets. Exclusive PR generates media buzz. Securing an App Store feature can provide a massive boost in organic downloads. As always, the key to success lies in the long term execution. These techniques have been proven across industries, but their effectiveness depends on delivering real value to users — and that's something only you can control. By integrating and testing different growth tactics, you can build a sustainable framework for app success. Every app is unique! So experiment, track results, and iterate to find what works best. With persistence and smart execution, your app can definitely stand out in today's crowded marketplace.
